cuttle_gaps.risk: None to stealth - Page.handleJavaScriptDialog is a pure CDP action with no page-visible trace. Only ordering risk: if a driver has its own dialog listener (playwright-cli does), whoever answers first wins and the loser gets InvalidParams. Return that as a benign 'already handled' rather than a 500.

cuttle_gaps.gap: cuttle's humanizer happily drives a renderer that is frozen behind a dialog, and pays full timeouts doing it. handleMouse -> awaitStable (humanize.go:794) issues Runtime.evaluate probes bounded by queryTimeout = 2s (humanize.go:83) and is explicitly fail-open ('ANY doubt ... returns immediately, so a click is never blocked'), so it burns 2s, learns nothing, and presses anyway; verifyToggle (humanize.go:826) then polls the same dead expression for the whole togglePollBudget; typing paces ~130ms/char into a page that cannot receive it. The agent sees slow no-ops, which is exactly the 'keeps poking the DOM' symptom.
cuttle_gaps.what_to_build: Give humanizer a pointer to the per-seed dialogState from gap 1 (thread it through cdpSessionOpts in wsproxy.go:115, alongside keepAliveID/locale). In handleClientFrame (humanize.go:385), when a dialog is pending on this seed, short-circuit Input.dispatchMouseEvent / dispatchKeyEvent / insertText and answer the driver with a CDP error instead of dispatching: `{"error":{"code":-32000,"message":"cuttle: a beforeunload JS dialog is blocking this page: \"...\" - clear it with POST /dialogs/{seed}/handle or `cuttle dialog accept`"}}`. Skip the probes entirely (do not pay queryTimeout).

Keep the check keyed on the seed and, once cuttle tracks per-target sessions, on the target - copy agent-browser's rule that a background-tab dialog must not block the active tab.

cuttle_gaps.gap: A dialog opened by a mousedown handler strands cuttle's pointer state. humanize.go:447 forwards mousePressed under the driver's own id and returns; the browser's ack never arrives (the renderer is blocked), the driver times out and aborts, and cuttle keeps haveClick=true / lastPressCX,lastPressCY set while Chrome keeps the left button logically DOWN. The next click is then interpreted as a drag or a double-click - a silent, seed-persistent corruption of exactly the humanized input that is cuttle's differentiator.
cuttle_gaps.what_to_build: In humanize.go, race the press: after forwarding mousePressed, wait on either the browser's ack or the seed's dialogState transitioning to open. On the dialog branch, record a pendingRelease{sid, x, y, button} on the humanizer, answer the driver with the gap-3 error, and dispatch the injected mouseReleased the moment POST /dialogs/{seed}/handle resolves the dialog (reuse h.inject + tightClickParams("mouseReleased", ..., buttons:0)). Reset haveClick/lastPress on that path.

themes.theme: Getting text - especially secrets (passwords, OTPs, API keys) - reliably into a field without the value entering the agent's transcript and without the field silently rejecting or resetting it
themes.state_of_the_art:
Four distinct mechanisms exist upstream, and no single project has all four. cuttle has none of them at the daemon layer - it delegates the whole theme to whichever driver the agent picked.

1) NAME-SUBSTITUTION + OUTPUT REDACTION (microsoft/playwright-cli, via bundled playwright-core 1.63.0-alpha in `playwright-core/lib/coreBundle.js`). `PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_SECRETS_FILE` is loaded by `dotenvFileLoader` into `config.secrets` (coreBundle.js:71420). Two methods on the context implement the whole feature: `lookupSecret(name)` (L64439) returns `{value, code}` - the real value plus `process.env['NAME']` as the code to print - falling back to the literal string when the name is unknown; `redactSecrets(text)` (L64447) is a plain `text.replaceAll(secretValue, '<secret>NAME</secret>')`. Redaction is applied at exactly three chokepoints: progress/call-log lines (L63386), file writes of output (L64686), and text results returned to the client (L64765). Only two tools consume `lookupSecret`: `browser_fill_form` (L65640, `locator.fill(secret.value)`) and `browser_type` (L65733, `locator.fill` or `pressSequentially` when `slowly:true`). That is why cuttle's own SKILL.md is right that a secret cannot ride a scripted `eval`/`run-code` block. Crucially, the value DOES enter Playwright's internal call log verbatim - `_fill` does `progress.log(\`  fill("${value}")\`)` right before `injected.fill` - and is scrubbed only on the way out, only for values registered in the secrets file.

2) AN ENCRYPTED LOCAL VAULT + AN OUT-OF-PROCESS CREDENTIAL PLUGIN (vercel-labs/agent-browser). `cli/src/native/auth.rs` stores `AuthProfile{name,url,username,password,username_selector,password_selector,submit_selector}` AES-256-GCM-encrypted under `~/.agent-browser/auth/<name>.json`, key from `AGENT_BROWSER_ENCRYPTION_KEY` or an auto-generated `~/.agent-browser/.encryption-key` (dir 0700, key file 0600). `agent-browser auth save <name> --password-stdin` keeps the value off argv and out of shell history. `agent-browser auth login <name>` (`cli/src/native/actions.rs:10668 handle_auth_login`) then does the whole flow inside the daemon: navigate, resolve fields, fill, click submit, wait for navigation - so the password never crosses the CLI/LLM boundary at all. For a real vault, `cli/src/plugins.rs` defines the `agent-browser.plugin.v1` stdio protocol with a `credential.read` capability; `resolve_credential_with_plugins` shells out to e.g. a 1Password/Vault plugin and gets back `ResolvedCredential{username,password,url,otp,usernameSelector,passwordSelector,submitSelector}` just-in-time, never persisted (`docs/src/app/security/page.mdx`: "Plugin credentials are resolved just-in-time and are not saved locally"), gated by `--confirm-actions plugin:vault:credential.read`. Note the `otp` field is declared in `plugins.rs:47` but never read anywhere in the tree - agent-browser's OTP story is aspirational, and its own docs (`skill-data/core/references/authentication.md`, "Two-Factor Authentication") punt 2FA to a human in a headed window plus `state save`.

3) FIELD-RESOLUTION AND CLEAR-BEFORE-TYPE THAT ACTUALLY SURVIVES REAL LOGIN PAGES. agent-browser's `wait_for_any_selector` (`actions.rs:10565`) polls a 16-entry preferred username-selector ladder (`input[type=email]`, `autocomplete=username`, `name*=user i`, ...) inside a bounded window, then falls back to `input[type=text]`, and its visibility predicate rejects zero-rect, `visibility:hidden`, `display:none`, `opacity:0`, `:disabled`, `type=hidden` and `readOnly` elements - i.e. it will not fill a decoy field. CloakHQ/CloakBrowser takes the opposite, human-shaped route: `cloakbrowser/human/__init__.py:1201 _human_fill` runs actionability (`CHECKS_INPUT` = attached/visible/enabled/**editable**/pointer_events), waits a `field_switch_delay`, performs a real humanized CLICK into the field, then `Ctrl/Cmd+A`, `Backspace`, then `human_type` character by character (`cloakbrowser/human/keyboard.py`) - never `insertText` for ASCII, with per-char shift handling for symbols via explicit `Digit1`/`Minus`/`Quote` codes + windows VK codes, and `insertText` reserved only for non-ASCII. Playwright's own `injected.fill` is the middle ground: for text/password/email/etc it only `selectText()`s and returns `"needsinput"`, and the server then does `keyboard.insertText(value)` (or `press('Delete')` for empty) - a single IME-path edit, one `input` event, no keystrokes; it verifies nothing afterwards (the one `if (input.value !== value) throw 'Malformed value'` check exists only for the setValue types: color/date/time/range/week).

4) A CLIPBOARD PATH THAT NEVER TOUCHES CDP OR THE TRANSCRIPT (CloakHQ/CloakBrowser-Manager - the closest analogue to cuttle, same KasmVNC + one-Chrome-per-profile shape). `backend/main.py:643 POST /api/profiles/{id}/clipboard` pipes the text into `xclip -selection clipboard` with `DISPLAY=:<profile display>`, keeps the xclip process alive so it can serve the paste, and kills the previous one per display (`_xclip_procs`). `GET .../clipboard` (L679) reads back via CDP because Chrome under KasmVNC never writes the X11 selection. The VNC leg is bridged in the RFB proxy: `_parse_kasmvnc_clipboard` (L204) decodes KasmVNC's non-standard BinaryClipboard message type 180 (`type(1)+action(1)+flags(4)`, then `mime_len(u8)+mime+data_len(u32be)+data` entries) and re-emits it as standard RFB ServerCutText type 3 (`_build_server_cut_text`, latin-1 per spec); the viewer (`frontend/src/components/ProfileViewer.tsx:96-143`) intercepts Ctrl/Cmd+V, pushes the host clipboard through `api.setClipboard` FIRST, then lets noVNC deliver the keystroke. agent-browser has the poor-man's version: `handle_clipboard` (`cli/src/native/actions.rs:7765`) - `write` = `navigator.clipboard.writeText(...)` via `evaluate` (so the value lands in the daemon command JSON), `paste` = `press_key_with_modifiers("v", Meta|Ctrl)`.

5) THE STEALTH-LAYER ANSWER (clearcotelabs/clearcote-browser). Rather than humanize CDP, it moves input into the browser process: `patches/130-humanized-input.patch` adds `Browser.humanizedClick`/`humanizedClickSelector` that build `WebMouseEvent` with `kNoModifiers` and route via `RenderWidgetHostInputEventRouter` - the patch comment is literally "No kFromDebugger marker - we want this to look like real input" (L276, L1482, L2868). `docs/PATCHES.md:158` specs the keyboard twin that has not been built yet: `humanize-cdp-keyboard-timing` / a browser-level `Input.humanizedType` with per-key gaussian dwell+flight, "Non-`kFromDebugger` path", parameters seeded per-eTLD+1 so the distribution is not profilable. `patches/200-agent-and-humanized-input.patch:536` shows the third option: route typing through Chrome's own Actor framework, `actor::TypeToolRequest(tab_handle, node_target(), text, enter, Mode::kReplace)` - browser-native replace-and-type against a DOM node id, no CDP Input at all. `docs/PATCHES.md:157` explicitly warns that the CDP `Input.dispatchMouseEvent` humanizer "still carries `kFromDebugger` via `CreateWebMouseEvent`" and should be treated as the fallback - which is exactly the path every one of cuttle's synthesized keystrokes takes today.

The daemon is the one component every driver's keystrokes pass through (wsproxy.go -> humanize.go), yet it has zero knowledge of secrets. Consequence: the redaction/substitution guarantee SKILL.md promises exists ONLY for playwright-cli. An agent on agent-browser or browser-use has no substitution and no redaction at all - it must inline the literal value into argv. And even on playwright-cli, redaction is a post-hoc `String.replaceAll` over OUTPUT, so any value not registered in the dotenv file (a code read off the page, a token from a previous step) is unprotected everywhere.

(a) Storage: `cuttle secrets set NAME` reading the value from stdin only (never argv - copy agent-browser's `--password-stdin`), held in the daemon's memory keyed per-seed and mirrored 0600 under dataDir/secrets/<seed>.json via the existing internal/atomicfile + the stateStore pattern in internal/serve/state.go:150-157 (0700 dir, 0600 file). Expose it as `PUT /profile/{seed}/secrets/{name}` next to the existing state routes in internal/serve/http.go:60-61. (b) Substitution: in humanize.go handleInsertText (L582) and handleKey (L498), before any keystroke goes out, if the text is exactly a sentinel (`{{cuttle:NAME}}`), swap in the real value and type THAT. Every driver bottoms out in Input.insertText through this proxy, so this makes the feature driver-agnostic - playwright's own call log then only ever contains the sentinel, which is strictly better than its own redaction. (c) Redaction: in wsproxy.go's browser->client path, before forwarding a frame, replace any registered secret value with `<secret>NAME</secret>` - the exact mechanic of playwright's redactSecrets, but applied to the CDP wire so it also covers Runtime.evaluate results, Network.getResponseBody and DOM snapshots from ANY driver. cuttle_gaps.gap: The humanizer's insertText rewrite blows playwright-cli's DEFAULT action timeout for any value longer than ~38 characters, and the cap is sized against a timeout that does not exist. humanize.go:150-156 sets insertTextMaxRunes=80 with the comment "a cap-length value already runs ~10s and a longer one would hold the driver's single pending command past its action timeout". But playwright-cli's default is 5000ms (`--timeout-action ... defaults to 5000ms`, README.md:558 / PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_TIMEOUT_ACTION), and playwright's `_fill` races `keyboard.insertText` inside the same progress deadline as the actionability check. At the measured pacing (interKeyDelay mean 0.97*85*e^(0.35^2/2) + 0.03*520 = 103ms, keyHold 24*e^(0.30^2/2) = 25ms, typo roll ~5ms = ~133ms/char) the 5s budget is exhausted at 37 characters. So every value between ~38 and 80 runes - i.e. exactly the API-key/long-password band - times out the driver. Worse, cuttle keeps typing after the driver gave up (h.sleep only aborts on connection teardown, not on an abandoned request id), so the agent sees a failure, retries fill, and the value is typed TWICE into a field that already had it. That is precisely the reported symptom "agents fumble ... even simple typing into fields" and "the field silently rejects or resets the input".
cuttle_gaps.what_to_build: Three changes, all small. (1) Lower insertTextMaxRunes to a value the DEFAULT driver timeout actually admits - ~30 runes at 133ms/char leaves headroom for the actionability check that runs inside the same budget. (2) Add the timeout to the attach line cuttle prints: internal/cli/drivers.go:59 is `playwright-cli attach --cdp={cdp}`; make it `PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_TIMEOUT_ACTION=30000 playwright-cli attach --cdp={cdp}` so a humanized fill fits, and say why in one clause. This is the single highest-leverage line in the repo for this theme - the briefing is what the agent copies. (3) Make abandonment safe: when handleInsertText's typing loop is still running and the client sends any new command on the same session, or a per-command wall-clock budget expires, stop typing and answer with a CDP error naming how many runes landed - a half-typed field the agent KNOWS about is recoverable; one it does not know about is not.

The coherent variant is to make the cap a function of the negotiated budget rather than a constant - default to the conservative ~30 and raise it when the connection URL carries an explicit opt-in (e.g. `?typing-budget-ms=`), which the briefing sets alongside the raised driver timeout.

Emit only a boolean plus the observed length. On mismatch: retry once (re-select the field with Ctrl/Cmd+A and retype, which is what cloakbrowser's fill does unconditionally) and, if it still mismatches, answer the driver's insertText with a CDP error naming the discrepancy (`typed 24 runes, field holds 18`). themes.theme: An agent seeing the page: screenshots, aria/a11y snapshots, element refs, change diffs, and getting an image or snapshot out of a remote containerised browser
themes.state_of_the_art:
Three distinct layers exist in these projects, and cuttle currently occupies none of them.

**1. Page-level "seeing" is a driver concern, and both drivers converge on the same design.** playwright-cli (`skills/playwright-cli/SKILL.md`) makes the aria snapshot the DEFAULT return value of every command ("After each command, playwright-cli provides a snapshot of the current browser state"), writes it to `.playwright-cli/page-<ts>.yml` on the driver host, and explicitly demotes images: "take a screenshot (rarely used, as snapshot is more common)". Refs are `e15` tokens minted by `injected.ariaSnapshotJSON()` inside Playwright's utility (isolated) world and resolved back through the `aria-ref=e15` selector engine; iframes are pierced by re-entering with `aria-ref=<ref> >> internal:control=enter-frame >> body,frameset` (`packages/playwright-core/src/server/page.ts`, `ariaSnapshotJSONForFrame`). Options that matter for token cost: `--depth=N`, `--boxes` (emits `[box=x,y,w,h]`, the bridge from a ref to a coordinate), `snapshot e34` for a partial re-snapshot, and `find "text" / --regex` which greps the snapshot server-side and returns matching nodes with 3 lines of context instead of the whole tree. agent-browser reimplements the same thing in Rust over raw CDP (`cli/src/native/snapshot.rs`, 1601 lines): `Accessibility.enable` + `Accessibility.getFullAXTree`, roles bucketed into INTERACTIVE/CONTENT/STRUCTURAL, refs `@e1` backed by a `RefMap {backend_node_id, role, name, nth, selector, frame_id}` (`element.rs`). Its one genuine discovery over a pure AX tree is `find_cursor_interactive_elements` (`snapshot.rs:624`): a page-side scan for `getComputedStyle(el).cursor === 'pointer'` / `onclick` / `tabindex`, de-duplicated against inherited pointer cursors, plus `promote_hidden_inputs` — this recovers the div-with-onclick and the visually-hidden `<input>` behind a styled label that the AX tree either omits or reports with an empty name. Both agree refs die on every page change.

**2. Screenshots are CDP-native and deliberately avoid viewport emulation.** Playwright: `Page.captureScreenshot({format, quality, clip, captureBeyondViewport: !fitsViewport})` with `clip` derived from `Page.getLayoutMetrics` (`chromium/crPage.ts:296`) — no `Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride`, so the page never observes a resize. agent-browser's `screenshot.rs` is the same shape (`Page.getLayoutMetrics` -> `contentSize` -> `clip` + `captureBeyondViewport` for full page; a `Runtime.callFunctionOn` bounding-rect clip for element shots), plus `--annotate`: it resolves every `RefMap` entry via batched `DOM.resolveNode` + `getBoundingClientRect`, injects a numbered overlay div, captures, removes the overlay, and returns `annotations[{ref, number, role, name, box}]` alongside the image so a multimodal model can map label `[N]` back to ref `@eN`.

**3. Everything a page screenshot CANNOT show is handled out of band.** This is where cuttle's peers diverge from cuttle. `Page.captureScreenshot` never contains browser chrome or a native JS dialog, so agent-browser instead makes dialogs a first-class daemon state machine: a background task auto-accepts `alert`/`beforeunload` while leaving `confirm`/`prompt` for the agent (`actions.rs:791 start_dialog_handler`), a `pending_dialog` field is set from `Page.javascriptDialogOpening` and cleared on `javascriptDialogClosed` (`actions.rs:1700`), every page-touching command fails fast with instructions while a dialog is open on the ACTIVE tab (`actions.rs:2411`), every response is stamped with `warning: "A JavaScript {type} dialog is blocking the page: ... use dialog accept/dismiss"` (`actions.rs:2690`), `tab list` reports `"dialogBlocked": true` per tab, autosave is suppressed because the storage evaluate would hang (`actions.rs:3893`), and `dispatch_mouse_or_dialog` (`interaction.rs:936`) `tokio::select!`s the `Input.dispatchMouseEvent` ack against `Page.javascriptDialogOpening` precisely because "a synchronous dialog blocks the renderer's main thread, so the input ack cannot arrive". When that happens the pointer is left logically down and a `pending_pointer_release` is dispatched once the dialog clears (`actions.rs:7295`). The same philosophy covers overlays: `BLOCKER_AT_JS` (`element.rs:731`) hit-tests the click point (descending same-origin iframes, walking shadow hosts, excusing label/control pairs) and turns a covered target into `"Element '<sel>' is covered by <div#consent-banner> at its click point ... Dismiss or interact with the covering element first"` (`element.rs:824`) rather than a silent mis-click.

**4. Getting pixels out of a remote/containerised browser.** agent-browser's answer for a sandboxed browser is crude — `screenshot --json` writes a file inside the sandbox, then `base64` it back over the exec channel (`skill-data/vercel-sandbox/SKILL.md:37`). Its live-view answer is `Page.startScreencast{format:jpeg, quality:80, maxWidth, everyNthFrame:1}` fanned out over a WebSocket to a dashboard, with frames on a `watch` channel (latest-wins) and everything else on an ordered broadcast (`stream/cdp_loop.rs`). CloakBrowser-Manager, the closest structural analogue to cuttle, solves the container-viewer problem at the X layer instead: `VNCManager.allocate()` hands each profile its own display (`:100+n`) and websocket port (`6100+n`), and `start_vnc` runs `Xvnc :N -geometry {profile.screen_width}x{profile.screen_height} -websocketPort N -rfbport -1 -httpd ... -interface 127.0.0.1` (`backend/vnc_manager.py:52-80`), launching the browser with `DISPLAY=:N` and `viewport = screen_height - 133` (`backend/browser_manager.py:260-306`), then proxying the RFB websocket through its own FastAPI (`backend/main.py`, with a full RFB message-boundary filter for KasmVNC's forked dialect). One display per identity, sized to that identity's spoofed screen — the framebuffer matches the window by construction. For change detection, agent-browser has both halves in `native/diff.rs`: `diff_snapshots` (Myers via the `similar` crate, unified diff with `context_radius(3)`, plus additions/removals/unchanged counts and an identity fast path) and `diff_screenshot` (per-pixel RGB distance against `threshold*255*sqrt(3)`, dimmed-grayscale base with red-flagged differing pixels, explicit `dimension_mismatch` result).

cuttle today: `internal/serve/http.go:53-65` exposes exactly `/`, `/json/version`, `/json/list`, `/profile/{seed}/state`, `/downloads`, `/downloads/{name}`, and the two devtools WS routes. There is no screenshot, snapshot, a11y, dialog, or diff code anywhere in `internal/` (a repo-wide grep for `captureScreenshot|getFullAXTree|javascriptDialogOpening|beforeunload` returns zero hits outside the humanizer's aria-toggle strings). The daemon holds no persistent CDP connection to a seed — it dials on demand (`keepalive.go:createKeepAlivePage`, `supervise.go` -> `internal/cdp`) — so nothing is observing a seed between driver attachments. What cuttle does have that its peers lack is the ideal seam for all of this: every CDP frame in both directions already passes through `proxyCDPWebsocket` (`internal/serve/wsproxy.go`) with an established idiom for injecting proxy-owned commands (`sendInjected`/`swallowInjected`, id floor 2e9), synthesising client responses (`keepAliveCloseResponse`, `blockContextCreation`), and rewriting browser->client frames (`stampSWContext`, `hideKeepAlive`); it knows whether any driver is attached (`pool.conns[seedKey]`, `pool.go:163-177`); it already runs `document.elementFromPoint` at every click point in an isolated world (`humanize.go:probeExpr`); and the image already ships KasmVNC 1.3.3 (`ops/docker/Dockerfile`, `ARG KASMVNC_VERSION=1.3.3`), whose documented developer API includes `GET /api/get_screenshot?width&height&quality&dedup` on the very port cuttle already publishes as the viewer (6080).

This is the literal mechanism behind pain #4 - the 'Leave site? Changes you made may not be saved' dialog is browser UI, so it is invisible to the DOM AND invisible to every screenshot the driver can take. The human at the VNC viewer can see it; the agent structurally cannot.

In internal/cli/commands.go add `cuttle screenshot [dest]` mirroring the existing `cuttle downloads [name [dest]]` verb, defaulting dest to a timestamped file in cwd and printing the absolute path so the agent can Read it. Pass `dedup=1` to get a 16-char XXH64 hash instead of bytes when nothing changed since the last call - a near-free 'did anything change since my last action' probe. Return a clear 503 with the reason when CUTTLE_VNC != 1. Document it in internal/cli/SKILL.md as the tool to reach for the moment a driver reports a hang or an unexplained no-op.

Two real caveats to encode: (a) it only exists when CUTTLE_VNC=1, so the verb must fail loudly rather than silently return nothing in headless-farm mode; (b) it captures the WHOLE 1920x1080 desktop including every other seed's overlapping window, which is a privacy/leak consideration in a multi-seed container and an argument for the per-seed display in the gap below. Page.javascriptDialogOpening fires exactly once, at the browser, to whoever is attached - so a dialog raised while no driver is connected (during a VNC handoff, between two `playwright-cli` invocations, after a driver crash) is永 invisible to the next driver that attaches: there is no CDP command to query a pending dialog. The renderer main thread is blocked for as long as it stands, so every subsequent evaluate, snapshot and actionability wait hangs, which is exactly the 'keep poking the DOM against a blocked page' symptom.

(4) Auto-resolve only when `p.conns[seedKey] == 0` (pool.go already tracks this): accept `beforeunload` and `alert` after a short grace period so an unattended seed can never wedge, and never auto-answer `confirm`/`prompt` - leave those for the human at the viewer or the next driver.

cuttle_gaps.gap: The humanizer serialises the entire client->browser direction and blocks on renderer-bound probes, so a JS dialog stalls the very commands that would clear it, and no code path races the dialog event against an input ack. preprocessClient runs inline in the client reader goroutine (wsproxy.go, `wg.Go(func(){ for { clientWS.Read; preprocessClient; cdpSend } })`), and handleMouse calls h.awaitStable -> h.query (Runtime.evaluate, queryTimeout 2s) and h.verifyToggle (up to 600ms of polling) synchronously. With a dialog open the renderer never answers those evaluates, so each click burns its full timeout while every other frame the driver sends - including its Page.handleJavaScriptDialog - waits behind it. Separately, a dialog opened by the mousedown handler means Chrome never acks the forwarded Input.dispatchMouseEvent, so the driver's click() hangs to its own timeout, and cuttle leaves the button logically down (h.haveClick / lastPress state), so the next click can register as a drag or double-click.

themes.theme: Files crossing the container boundary: page downloads out, file uploads in (input[type=file], CDP file chooser, drag-drop), PDFs, and save-as dialogs
themes.state_of_the_art:
Three distinct mechanisms exist in the wild, and the projects differ mainly in which side of the boundary they assume the filesystem is on.

**1. Playwright (microsoft/playwright, the engine under playwright-cli) has TWO upload paths and only one of them survives a remote browser.** In `packages/playwright-core/src/server/dom.ts` `_setInputFiles` (~L726-762): when the caller passed *paths*, Playwright does `fs.promises.access(localPath)` on the **driver host**, then `this._page.delegate.setInputFilePaths(...)` -> `crPage.ts:337` sends `DOM.setFileInputFiles {files: [<driver-host path>]}`. When the caller passed *buffers* (`filePayloads`), it instead does `retargeted.evaluateInUtility(([injected, node, files]) => injected.setInputFiles(node, files))` - the File objects are constructed **inside the page**, so no filesystem is involved. `_drop` (dom.ts ~L659-724) always takes the buffer route: it base64s the file on the driver host and builds a `DataTransfer` + `DragEvent` sequence in the page's main world. Net effect against a containerized browser: `playwright-cli drop <ref> --path=<file>` works, `playwright-cli upload <file>` does not - Chrome inside the container gets a path that does not exist there.

**2. Playwright's file-chooser interception is what makes upload "one step".** `packages/playwright-core/src/tools/backend/tab.ts:125` registers a `filechooser` listener on every page, which flips `Page.setInterceptFileChooserDialog {enabled:true}` (`crPage.ts:1052 _updateFileChooserInterception`, event handled at `crPage.ts:905`). The chooser is then surfaced as a *modal state* the snapshot prints as `- [File chooser]: can be handled by browser_file_upload`, and `tools/backend/files.ts` `uploadFile` consumes it (`clearsModalState: 'fileChooser'`). Two consequences: the native GTK dialog **never renders**, and the agent is told, in the snapshot, that a chooser is waiting. Same file also ships `browser_drop` with `paths`/`data`, and the config gates paths with `allowUnrestrictedFileAccess` / MCP roots.

**3. Downloads: Playwright auto-saves and logs; agent-browser makes click-to-file one verb.** `tab.ts:135` listens for `download`, and `_downloadStarted` (L219-231) immediately `download.saveAs(outputFile)` into the MCP output dir and emits `download-start` / `download-finish` log entries into the tool response. agent-browser goes further with a single verb: `cli/src/native/actions.rs` `handle_download` (~L6440-6590) = `Browser.setDownloadBehavior {behavior:"allowAndName", eventsEnabled:true, downloadPath:<dir>}` -> click the selector -> loop on `Browser.downloadWillBegin` (capture `guid`) and `Browser.downloadProgress` until `state=="completed"` -> `fs::rename(dir/<guid>, dest)`, with a 10x100ms retry because Chrome flushes after signalling completion, plus a fallback when the GUID capture missed. `handle_waitfordownload` (~L9360) is the standalone `wait --download`. agent-browser also re-applies `setDownloadBehavior` to every context it creates (actions.rs ~L6711) because the launch-time call only covers the default context. Upload in agent-browser is `browser.rs:1901 upload_files` -> `DOM.describeNode` for the `backendNodeId` -> `DOM.setFileInputFiles` - host paths again; its sandboxed wrapper is honest about it: `packages/@agent-browser/eve/extension/tools/upload.ts` says "Paths refer to files inside the sandbox (e.g. under /workspace)". That is the only correct model for a remote browser: get the bytes into the browser's filesystem first, then hand it a path.

**4. PDFs never touch a filesystem.** `crPdf.ts:104` sends `Page.printToPDF {transferMode:'ReturnAsStream'}` and reads the bytes back with `IO.read`. This is protocol-only, works headed, and is inherently boundary-crossing. clearcote's MCP (`mcp/clearcote_mcp/server.py:277-288`, `_facade.py:181-188`) takes the weaker route - `page.screenshot(path=)` / `page.pdf(path=)` written into a `_confine_path`-guarded sandbox dir, with an explicit "headless only" comment on pdf.

**5. Nobody gets upload from the VNC layer.** KasmVNC ships a read-only `/api/downloads` listing in Xvnc's mini-httpd, but has no upload feature at all (kasmtech/KasmVNC#250 - "KasmVNC itself has no file upload/download feature; Kasm Workspaces does"). CloakBrowser-Manager (the closest architectural analogue: KasmVNC + per-profile Chromium in one container) has *no* file-boundary story whatsoever - grep for download/upload in `backend/browser_manager.py` and `backend/main.py` only hits binary self-download.

**Where that leaves cuttle.** cuttle's *download-out* path is arguably ahead of the pack: `internal/serve/pool.go` `seedProfileDefaults`/`pinDownloadDir` (~L813-880) pins `download.default_directory` + `prompt_for_download:false` + `savefile.default_directory` in Chrome's own **Preferences** rather than over CDP, which is what makes it survive a driver attach; `internal/serve/downloads.go` serves `GET /downloads` (hiding `.crdownload` partials) and `GET /downloads/{name}` (bare-basename guard, `nosniff`, forced attachment); `internal/cli/commands.go:917-1010` `cuttle downloads [name [dest]]` pulls to 0600 and prints only the path. That beats `download.saveAs()`, which cannot work over `connectOverCDP` at all. But cuttle has **zero upload path** (no hit for `setFileInputFiles`, `fileChooser`, `upload`, or `printToPDF` anywhere in `internal/` or `cmd/`), no download completion signal, and no guard on drivers that redirect the download directory out from under it.

cuttle_gaps.gap: cuttle has no way to get a file from the agent's host INTO the container, so every path-based upload API in every driver is broken against it. `rg -n -i 'upload|setFileInputFiles|chooser' internal/ cmd/` returns nothing but a comment about the state-PUT body cap. `playwright-cli upload ./doc.pdf` and `agent-browser upload @e1 doc.pdf` both end in `DOM.setFileInputFiles {files:['/Users/…/doc.pdf']}` sent to a Chrome that has no such path.

Small compatibility risk: a driver legitimately referencing a container-internal path it created itself will still stat fine, so the guard is a strict improvement. cuttle_gaps.gap: cuttle never enables `Page.setInterceptFileChooserDialog`, so a click on an `<input type=file>` opens a real GTK file-chooser window on the Xvfb/Xvnc display (libgtk-3-0 is installed in the image). The page is then blocked behind a modal the agent cannot see and cannot dismiss - the same blindness class as the beforeunload dialog the user already reports, and there is no cuttle-side record that a chooser is even waiting.

themes.theme: The human-viewable surface of a remote browser: framebuffer vs browser-window sizing, per-session viewer routing, dynamic resize (RandR / setDeviceMetricsOverride / Browser.setWindowBounds / Browser.setContentsSize), DPR, clipboard sync, and human takeover UX - without breaking window.inner* vs window.outer* vs screen.* coherence.
themes.state_of_the_art:
Three distinct approaches exist, and cuttle sits between two of them without taking either one's payoff.

1) CloakHQ/CloakBrowser-Manager - the closest analogue, and the one that actually solves "window fills the viewer". It gives EVERY profile its own KasmVNC display, sized to that profile's own spoofed screen, instead of one shared framebuffer. `~/pjv/cloakhq/cloakbrowser-manager/backend/vnc_manager.py` allocates `display = BASE_DISPLAY(100)+n`, `ws_port = BASE_WS_PORT(6100)+n` and starts `Xvnc :{display} -geometry {width}x{height} -depth 24 -websocketPort {ws_port} -rfbport -1 -SecurityTypes None -DisableBasicAuth -interface 127.0.0.1 -AlwaysShared -httpd /usr/share/kasmvnc/www`, where width/height come from the profile record. `backend/browser_manager.py:260-308` then launches Chrome with `env DISPLAY=:{display}` and `viewport = {screen_width, screen_height - 133}` (133 = the engine's frame: title/tab strip + toolbar), and `_build_fingerprint_args` (line 581) passes `--fingerprint-screen-width/-height` from the same record. Framebuffer == spoofed screen == window, by construction: the window fills the viewer AND `inner <= outer <= avail <= screen` holds. FastAPI proxies each display's websocket at `/api/profiles/{id}/vnc` (backend/main.py:~850) and translates KasmVNC BinaryClipboard type 180 into standard RFB ServerCutText (`_parse_kasmvnc_clipboard`, main.py:204), so one HTTP port fronts N displays. Its clipboard relay is two-way and CDP-backed, not X-backed: `POST /api/profiles/{id}/clipboard` pipes into `xclip -selection clipboard` (main.py:643-676), while `GET .../clipboard` reads the page instead, because - in their own words at main.py:683 - "Chrome doesn't write to X11 clipboard under KasmVNC, so xclip can't read it"; an init script (`browser_manager.py:351-370`) parks the last `copy`/selection text in `window.__clipboardText` and the endpoint evaluates it over CDP, with xclip only as a fallback. The React viewer (`frontend/src/components/ProfileViewer.tsx`) is stock noVNC with `scaleViewport=true, resizeSession=false`, plus a fullscreen toggle, a clipboard-sync toggle, a connect-state dot, and a 2s poll of the CDP clipboard endpoint.

2) ClearcoteLabs/clearcote-browser - the rigorous treatment of geometry coherence, as a shipped, tested SDK module rather than launch flags. `~/pjv/clearcotelabs/clearcote-browser/sdk/node/src/geometry.ts` (mirrored in `sdk/python/clearcote/_geometry.py`, `sdk/dotnet/src/Clearcote/Geometry.cs`) states the invariant as testable code: `geometryIsCoherent(screen, avail, inner, outer)` = `inner <= outer <= avail <= screen` on both axes. It splits two regimes: with a persona active, the engine's own screen spoof beats a CDP override, so the SDK sets `viewport: null` and then FITS THE REAL WINDOW to the persona work area over CDP - `fitWindowToPersona()` reads `[screen.availWidth, screen.availHeight]`, calls `Browser.getWindowForTarget` + `Browser.setWindowBounds`, re-reads `[outerWidth, outerHeight]`, and applies `fitPlan()`, which measures the shortfall (33px on 149) and adds it back rather than hardcoding it, with an overshoot guard that never leaves `outer > avail`. Without a persona it instead picks a screen from a real-capture corpus weighted by distinct /24 (`HEADLESS_SCREEN_PROFILES`: 1920x1080 w24, 2560x1440 w13, 1920x1200 w6, 1366x768 w3, 1600x900 w3, 3440x1440 w2 capped from 12, 3840x2160 w2, 1680x1050 w2) and sets `viewport = screen - (ENGINE_FRAME_WIDTH 8, ENGINE_FRAME_HEIGHT 131)` so the synthesized outer lands exactly on the screen edge, plus `moveWindowToOrigin()` because the headless default position (10,10) puts `screenX + outerWidth` past `screen.width` - a shape only 6% of real captures have. `test/geometry.test.ts` measures the live engine and fails on frame-delta drift. Separately, `patches/141-media-queries.patch` closes the CSS side that everyone else forgets: `MediaValues::CalculateDeviceWidth/CalculateDeviceHeight/CalculateDevicePixelRatio/CalculateDeviceSupportsHDR/CalculateColorBitsPerComponent/Calculate*PointerTypes/Calculate*HoverTypes/CalculateColorGamut` all read the persona instead of `display::ScreenInfo`.

3) vercel-labs/agent-browser and microsoft/playwright-cli - viewer surfaces built on CDP screencast instead of VNC, with real takeover UX. agent-browser's `cli/src/native/stream/` is a WebSocket viewer protocol: `cdp_loop.rs` auto-starts `Page.startScreencast {format:jpeg, quality, maxWidth, maxHeight, everyNthFrame:1}` on first client and stops on last; frames ride a latest-wins `watch` channel while status/tabs/url/console ride an ordered broadcast; `skill-data/core/references/streaming.md` documents `{"type":"config","pacing":"ack"}` (one frame in flight, cumulative acks, so a stalled client resumes on the CURRENT page not ten seconds of history), per-client `maxFps` 1-120, URL-declared `?pacing=ack&maxFps=10` for the opening frame, an origin allowlist on the upgrade, and measured budgets (q80 1280x720 ~54KB/frame, q20 ~25KB, q20@640x360 ~9KB). Input flows back as `input_mouse`/`input_keyboard`/`input_touch` dispatched on a task separate from frame delivery, and resets the idle timer. The dashboard (`packages/dashboard/src/components/viewport.tsx:313-320`) maps clicks with `scaleX = viewportWidth / rect.width` off `getBoundingClientRect()`, and a "fit" button calls `set viewport <canvasW> <canvasH>`; that command (`cli/src/native/browser.rs:1725-1777`) sends `Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride` AND THEN `Browser.setContentsSize` on the window, with the comment "Screencast captures the actual content area, not the emulated CSS viewport, so resize the content area to match" - i.e. `Browser.setContentsSize` is the CDP verb that sets the real content box directly, no frame arithmetic needed. playwright-cli's `playwright-cli show` (README:106-127) is the handoff UX benchmark: a session grid across workspaces with a live screencast thumbnail, name, URL and title per session, click to zoom into a detail view with tab bar, back/forward/reload/address bar, and "Click into the viewport to take over mouse and keyboard input; press Escape to release" - explicit, reversible takeover rather than an always-live canvas.

cuttle_gaps.gap: The X framebuffer is a fixed 1920x1080 while the browser window is deliberately sized DOWN to the seed's spoofed screen, so the window can never fill the viewer - and cuttle knows it, choosing coherence over fill. ops/docker/bin/docker-entrypoint.sh starts `Xvnc :99 -geometry 1920x1080`; internal/fingerprint/args.go:346 ScreenArgs emits `--window-size=<screen.w>,<screen.h - taskbar>`; internal/serve/pool.go:481 dropMaximizeIfSized strips the entrypoint's --start-maximized whenever a --window-size is pinned, with the comment 'The VNC entrypoint adds the flag purely so a human viewer gets a full-looking window, which is worth less than a coherent identity.' A 1366x768 seed therefore paints a 1366x720 window into a 1920x1080 canvas - 47% of the viewer is openbox grey. The same cap also truncates the persona table: args.go:298 restricts both screen tables to what fits 1920x1080, which excludes 2560x1440 - the second most common real desktop screen in clearcote's capture corpus (weight 13 of 55).
cuttle_gaps.what_to_build: Make the framebuffer follow the seed instead of the window following the framebuffer. Per-seed X display is the clean form (see the next gap); the minimal form that lands first: on the FIRST attach for a seed, have internal/serve/pool.go run `xrandr --newmode`/`--addmode`/`--output <out> --mode` (or KasmVNC's SetDesktopSize) against :99 to set the root window to exactly that seed's `screenSize`, keep `--window-size=<w>,<h-taskbar>` and `--window-position=0,0`, and let openbox place it at the origin. Then delete the '<= 1920x1080' constraint from screenChoicesWindows/screenChoicesMacOS in args.go and add 2560x1440 (regenerate golden.json via `just parity-golden`). Bump `Xvnc -geometry` to the largest table entry so RandR has headroom (Xvnc caps the session framebuffer at the largest startup mode).
cuttle_gaps.evidence: CloakHQ/CloakBrowser-Manager backend/vnc_manager.py:start_vnc(width=profile.screen_width, height=profile.screen_height) + backend/browser_manager.py:260-268,303-308 (Xvnc geometry == fingerprint screen == Chrome viewport). KasmVNC supports server-side resize (kasmweb.com/kasmvnc/docs/latest/configuration.html: desktop.resolution.width/height, desktop.allow_resize default true; clientside.html 'Remote Resizing'). Corpus weights: clearcote sdk/node/src/geometry.ts HEADLESS_SCREEN_PROFILES.
cuttle_gaps.risk: None to coherence if the resize targets the seed's OWN screen size - screen.* is spoofed by patch 0011 and does not read the X root window, so the framebuffer change is invisible to the page while making inner/outer/screen agree exactly as today. It is actively DANGEROUS to instead resize the framebuffer to the human's browser-tab size (KasmVNC 'Remote Resizing' / noVNC resizeSession=true), because then a maximized window would report an inner that no persona screen explains. Keep resizeSession=false in ops/docker/bin/vnc-viewer.html.

cuttle_gaps.gap: Every seed's Chrome shares one X display (:99) with one openbox desktop (ops/docker/Dockerfile:228-234 pins `<number>1</number>` desktops), and the viewer is a single un-parameterized URL (internal/cli/commands.go:68 defaultVNCPort = 6080; endpointURLs returns a bare http://127.0.0.1:6080/). With two or more seeds live, the human sees N overlapping Chrome windows and cannot tell which is the seed the agent asked them to log into, and `cuttle open --profile foo` does nothing to raise foo's window. This is the multiplexer's core promise (N identities behind one endpoint) failing at exactly the moment a human is needed.
cuttle_gaps.what_to_build: Two tiers. Cheap (ship first): after `cuttle open --profile <name>` resolves, have the daemon run `xdotool search --pid <seed chrome pid> --onlyvisible windowactivate windowraise` (xdotool is already installed, Dockerfile:217) so the named seed's window comes to the front, and print the seed name in the briefing's viewer line. Proper: give each seed its own Xvnc display like the manager does - allocate `:100+n` / an internal ws port per seed inside internal/serve/pool.go spawn(), pass `DISPLAY=:<n>` in the Chrome env, and add `GET /viewer/{seed}` + `GET /viewer/{seed}/websockify` routes to the existing mux in internal/serve/http.go:53-65 that reverse-proxy that seed's Xvnc, so 6080 keeps fronting everything and the entrypoint no longer owns the display.
cuttle_gaps.evidence: CloakHQ/CloakBrowser-Manager backend/vnc_manager.py (VNCManager.allocate: BASE_DISPLAY=100, BASE_WS_PORT=6100, one Xvnc per profile) and backend/main.py (`/api/profiles/{id}/vnc` websocket proxy, one HTTP port fronting N displays). microsoft/playwright-cli README:117-125 (`playwright-cli show` session grid: every session gets its own live tile with name + URL + title, click to zoom).
cuttle_gaps.risk: Per-seed displays multiply Xvnc processes and framebuffer RAM (~8MB per 1920x1080x24 plus KasmVNC encode buffers) on a memory-capped node - allocate a display lazily on first attach and tear it down with the seed's Chrome. No fingerprint surface changes: each seed already gets its own Chrome process; giving it its own display only removes a cross-seed observation channel (today two seeds can enumerate each other's X windows).

cuttle_gaps.gap: CSS media queries leak the REAL framebuffer and the REAL device pixel ratio, contradicting the JS spoof. cuttle's patch series patches screen.cc (packages/browser/patches/0011-screen-dimensions-from-cli.patch) and LocalDOMWindow outerWidth/outerHeight/devicePixelRatio (0013-window-outer-and-dpr.patch), but NOTHING patches blink's MediaValues. So `matchMedia('(min-device-width: 1920px)').matches` is true for a seed whose screen.width is 1366 (it reads display::ScreenInfo = the X root window), and on arm64 `window.devicePixelRatio === 2` (patch 0013 returns 2.0 for --fingerprint-platform=macos, set in args.go:80/197) while `matchMedia('(resolution: 2dppx)')` is false and `(-webkit-device-pixel-ratio: 2)` is false, because MediaValues::CalculateDevicePixelRatio still returns frame->DevicePixelRatio() = 1 under Xvnc. Both are single-expression, zero-cost checks for a detector.
cuttle_gaps.what_to_build: Port clearcote's 141-media-queries.patch into packages/browser/patches as a new numbered patch against third_party/blink/renderer/core/css/media_values.cc, keyed on the existing clark::seed values rather than a new switch: CalculateDeviceWidth -> clark::seed::Screen().width, CalculateDeviceHeight -> Screen().height, CalculateDevicePixelRatio -> the same platform-keyed constant patch 0013 uses. Add the three assertions (device-width, device-height, resolution/dppx vs devicePixelRatio) to packages/browser/validate and to test/smoke so the pair can never drift. Note the device-width/height half becomes moot for free if the framebuffer-per-seed change above lands; the DPR half does not - Xvnc rasters at 1x whatever the geometry.
cuttle_gaps.evidence: clearcotelabs/clearcote-browser patches/141-media-queries.patch (MediaValues::CalculateDeviceWidth/Height/DevicePixelRatio/SupportsHDR/ColorBitsPerComponent/PointerTypes/HoverTypes/ColorGamut all persona-keyed). Absent from both clark-labs-inc/clark-browser/patches and ~/Projects/cuttle/packages/browser/patches (grep for media_values returns nothing in either).
cuttle_gaps.risk: None - it removes an incoherence rather than adding a spoof. The one judgement call: matching DPR 2 in media queries means CSS `image-set`/`srcset` will fetch 2x assets that raster at 1x, which is exactly what a real Retina Mac does over a scaled remote desktop; the alternative (dropping the macOS DPR-2 spoof to 1) contradicts the Apple Silicon persona everywhere else. Prefer patching MediaValues. Regenerate golden.json only if arg output changes (it should not).

cuttle_gaps.gap: No post-launch geometry verification anywhere. cuttle computes the whole window/screen relationship at argv-build time (internal/fingerprint/args.go ScreenArgs) and never once measures what the live page actually reports; golden.json pins the ARGV, not the resulting inner/outer/avail/screen tuple. If openbox, a Chrome version bump, or a driver perturbs the window, cuttle finds out never. cuttle also never uses Browser.setWindowBounds or Browser.setContentsSize (zero hits across internal/).
cuttle_gaps.what_to_build: Add a coherence assertion to test/smoke: read `[screen.width, screen.height, screen.availWidth, screen.availHeight, innerWidth, innerHeight, outerWidth, outerHeight, screenX, screenY, devicePixelRatio]` off a real page and assert clearcote's chain `inner <= outer <= avail <= screen` on both axes, plus `screenX + outerWidth <= screen.width`, plus `matchMedia('(resolution: '+devicePixelRatio+'dppx)').matches`. Then add a one-shot fit in internal/serve/pool.go after the keep-alive tab attaches: `Browser.getWindowForTarget` -> `Browser.setContentsSize {width: screen.w, height: screen.h - taskbar - frame}` (setContentsSize sets the content box directly, so no frame-delta guessing), and log a warning rather than failing a launch if it does not converge.

cuttle_gaps.risk: None; it is a tripwire in the same spirit as golden.json. Keep the fit best-effort and silent-on-failure (clearcote's 'a geometry improvement must not be able to fail a launch') so a WM quirk cannot break `cuttle up`.

cuttle_gaps.gap: Nothing stops a driver from destroying the geometry the fingerprint layer just established. internal/serve/wsproxy.go intercepts Target.createBrowserContext (blocked by default), Fetch.enable/authRequired, Emulation.setLocaleOverride and Emulation.setFocusEmulationEnabled - but not Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride or Browser.setWindowBounds. agent-browser ships `set viewport` as a first-class verb, and its dashboard's fit button calls it on every resize; Playwright's `page.setViewportSize()` and any `browser.newContext()` after connectOverCDP do the same. The result is innerWidth 1280 inside a spoofed outerWidth of 1536 - 256px of window explained by no frame any real browser has - and, in the viewer, a letterboxed page inside an already-undersized window. cuttle's SKILL.md never mentions viewport at all.
cuttle_gaps.what_to_build: In internal/serve/wsproxy.go, add a guard alongside the existing createBrowserContext blocker: intercept `Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride` and `Emulation.clearDeviceMetricsOverride` and, unless an opt-out flag mirroring --allow-context-creation is set, answer with a CDP error naming the reason ('cuttle pins page geometry to the seed's screen; a viewport override desyncs window.inner* from the spoofed outer/screen'). Same treatment for Browser.setWindowBounds, or rewrite it to a clamped Browser.setContentsSize that can never exceed the seed's work area. Add a Geometry note to internal/cli/SKILL.md telling drivers not to set a viewport and to use viewport:null / no_viewport when they construct contexts.
cuttle_gaps.evidence: vercel-labs/agent-browser cli/src/native/browser.rs:1725-1777 (set_viewport = setDeviceMetricsOverride + Browser.setContentsSize) and packages/dashboard/src/components/viewport.tsx:290 (`set viewport <w> <h>` fired from the viewer's fit control). CloakHQ/CloakBrowser cloakbrowser/browser.py:210-274 defaults every headed context to no_viewport=True precisely so 'the page tracks the real window', and config.py:435-450 gates --start-maximized on binaries where maximizing cannot produce outerWidth < innerWidth.

Keep the escape hatch symmetric with the existing --allow-context-creation precedent, and make the rewrite-to-setContentsSize variant the default so the common case (a viewer asking the page to fill its canvas) still works while staying inside the seed's work area.

cuttle_gaps.gap: The VNC viewer is the only human surface, and it is all-or-nothing: no per-seed routing, no takeover/release model, no bandwidth control, no fit/1:1 toggle, no fullscreen button, no framerate or quality knob. ops/docker/bin/vnc-viewer.html hardcodes scaleViewport=true / resizeSession=false and downscales a 1920x1080 framebuffer into whatever tab the human has, so text is soft; over the ssh/k8s tunnel backends that is a full-framebuffer RFB stream with no pacing. There is also no lightweight preview an agent can use to show progress without a human sitting on the canvas.
cuttle_gaps.what_to_build: Two independent pieces. (a) Cheap viewer polish in vnc-viewer.html: a fullscreen button, a fit/1:1 toggle, and a connection-state dot - and, once the framebuffer matches the seed screen, prefer 1:1 with scroll over downscaling. (b) A CDP-screencast preview endpoint in internal/serve/http.go alongside the existing routes: `GET /preview/{seed}` upgrading to a WebSocket that runs Page.startScreencast on the seed's foreground tab and streams jpeg frames with agent-browser's ack pacing and per-client maxFps, read-only by default (no input path), so an agent or a dashboard can watch a run cheaply and only escalate to the VNC canvas for a real handoff. Page.startScreencast maxWidth/maxHeight only caps and letterboxes the encoded frame, which is stealth-neutral. PUT writes into the seed's X CLIPBOARD (xclip is a one-line Dockerfile add, or reuse the existing BinaryClipboard client path). GET reads it over CDP rather than over X: install a small init script per seed that parks the last `copy`/selection text in a page global, and evaluate it in an isolated world - falling back to xclip for non-Chrome owners. Then have the viewer's readBinaryClipboard path fall back to polling that endpoint when no type-180 message has arrived after a copy.

cuttle_gaps.gap: No dynamic-resize path exists at all, in either direction. `Xvnc -geometry 1920x1080` is fixed for the container's life (ops/docker/bin/docker-entrypoint.sh:28), the viewer pins `rfb.resizeSession = false` (vnc-viewer.html), and nothing in internal/ ever calls xrandr, RandR, SetDesktopSize, Browser.setWindowBounds or Browser.setContentsSize. Start Xvnc at the largest table entry so the session framebuffer cap is high enough. Explicitly do NOT expose a client-driven resize (keep resizeSession=false) and do not honor SetDesktopSize from the viewer.
cuttle_gaps.evidence: KasmVNC configuration docs (desktop.resolution.width/height, desktop.allow_resize default true) and clientside docs ('Remote Resizing - automatically resize the server-side resolution to fit the client's window size' vs 'Local Scaling'), kasmweb.com/kasmvnc/docs/latest/. LibVNC/x11vnc PR #107 documents the same server-side-framebuffer-plus-RANDR mechanism and its Xvfb-works/dummy-driver-does-not caveat.

themes.theme: Attaching to an existing browser and knowing where you are: CDP attach vs launch, proving attachment, target enumeration/selection, one-driver-at-a-time contention, tab lifecycle and ownership, browser-context semantics, crash/disconnect recovery, and session-inspection verbs.
themes.state_of_the_art:
The best-solved version of this theme lives in vercel-labs/agent-browser, and it is built on one insight: in a SHARED browser reached over CDP, "which tab am I on" is not derivable at attach time, so it must be PERSISTED and ENFORCED.

1) Persistent session-to-tab binding (agent-browser, PR #1589, v0.34.0). `~/pjv/vercel-labs/agent-browser/cli/src/native/tab_binding.rs` writes `{socket_dir}/{session}.target` = `{"targetId","url","pinned"}`. It deliberately outlives the daemon (unlike `.pid`/`.sock`), is written atomically (temp file, 0600, fsync, rename), and `load()` returns Err (not None) on a corrupt file because a corrupt file may have carried `pinned:true` and silently starting fresh would drop the isolation boundary. The persisted URL is sanitized (`sanitize_url`: creds/query/fragment stripped, opaque schemes like `data:`/`blob:` dropped) so a binding file never leaks a token.
   On attach, `apply_tab_binding_on_attach` (`cli/src/native/actions.rs:2774`) re-selects the bound target by targetId instead of adopting `Target.getTargets[0]` - the code comment names the exact failure: getTargets order is the browser's most recently active tab, "which in a shared browser is usually another session's tab" (issue #1530). If the bound target is gone and the session is pinned, the manager enters a `tab_gone` state (`browser.rs:1035 restore_target_binding`, `:1051 handle_bound_target_removed`) and EVERY page command fails with a machine-matchable `tab_gone:` prefix carrying `data.targetId` + optional `data.lastUrl`, while only `tab list` / `tab new` / `tab <ref>` still work as recovery verbs (`check_bound`, `browser.rs:993`). A pinned session with no binding opens a FRESH tab rather than adopting one. Tabs opened by the human or by another session are registered but never activated and never rebind (`add_page_without_activation` / `register_discovered_page`, `browser.rs:2017-2100`). If the binding cannot be persisted, the attach FAILS rather than pretending the pin is in place.
2) Target ids as the public tab handle. `tab_list()` (`browser.rs:1423`) emits `{tabId,targetId,label,title,url,type,active}`; `tab new --label <name>` names a tab; CDP target ids are accepted directly as tab refs because `t<N>` ids are per-daemon counters and target ids are stable across restarts (CHANGELOG entry for #1589).
3) Attach-time liveness proof rather than optimism. `discover_and_attach_targets` (`browser.rs:637`) does not `Page.enable` on target 0: Memory-Saver-discarded tabs keep a CDP session but have no renderer, so `Page.enable` never answers and connect hangs (#1036, #1528). It probes with a bounded `Runtime.evaluate("1")` (`renderer_responds`), picks a live tab, and only revives one browser-side (`ensure_renderer_alive`) if all are discarded; the pin-restore path calls `revive_and_enable_active` for the same reason. Connection health is checked with `is_connection_alive()` (bounded `Browser.getVersion`) and `has_process_exited()`.
4) Attached browsers are never torn down. `BrowserManager::close` (`browser.rs:1256`) sends `Browser.close` ONLY when it launched the process: "For external connections (--auto-connect, --cdp) we just disconnect without shutting down the user's browser." Playwright does the same structurally: in `packages/playwright-core/src/server/chromium/chromium.ts`, `_connectOverCDPImpl` wires `browserProcess = {close: doClose, kill: doClose}` to a transport close, while `attemptToGracefullyCloseBrowser` (which sends `Browser.close`) is reachable only on the launch path.
5) Attach/detach as first-class, separate verbs. microsoft/playwright-cli (README L271-277, `skills/playwright-cli/references/session-management.md`) splits `attach --cdp=<url|channel>` from `open`, and `detach` from `close`: "`detach` only works on sessions created via `attach`. For sessions created via `open`, use `close`." It has `list` (all sessions), `tab-list`/`tab-select <index>`/`tab-new`/`tab-close [index]`, and `show` (a dashboard to watch what agents are doing). Sessions are named (`-s=` / `PLAYWRIGHT_CLI_SESSION`) so parallel agents never collide on `default` - an attach by channel even auto-names the session after the channel.
6) The farm-side analogue, CloakHQ/CloakBrowser-Manager, is close to cuttle but weaker: `backend/main.py:910-1086` is a dumb bidirectional CDP passthrough with `/json/version` + `/json/list` URL rewriting (same shape as cuttle's `internal/serve/http.go`). What it does add is lifecycle hygiene cuttle can borrow: `POST /launch` returns 409 when already running, `launch()` rejects caller args that collide with manager-owned debugging (`--remote-debugging-port/-address`, `browser_manager.py:270`), stale `SingletonLock/Cookie/Socket` are cleared only in the container runtime, an `on_disconnected` handler (`_on_browser_closed`) reclaims ports/displays after a crash or human close, and inspection is split into an unauthenticated side-effect-free `/api/health` vs an auth-gated `/api/status` and a per-profile `/api/profiles/{id}/status` that reports `stopped` WITHOUT launching anything.
7) The engines contribute one attach-relevant item: clark's `patches/0047-suppress-cdc-globals.patch` blocks `cdc_*`/`__webdriver*`/`__selenium*` globals a CDP/ChromeDriver client can inject - but it registers the V8 extension in `headless/lib/renderer/headless_content_renderer_client.cc`, i.e. headless-only, so it is inert for cuttle's headed Xvfb runtime. clearcote frames the same area as "CDP side-effects" (README L239: `Runtime.enable` leaks, main-world execution) and says the client layer must hold them back via isolated worlds - which cuttle already does for its own probes (`internal/serve/humanize.go:1036`).

cuttle_gaps.gap: cuttle has no notion of which attached client owns which tab. Every ws connection to a seed (internal/serve/wsproxy.go serveWS) gets the same browser endpoint, the same default context, and the full target list; the pool only counts connections (chromePool.conns, pool.go connect/disconnect). 'One driver at a time' and 'Your tab is not tab 0' exist only as prose in internal/cli/SKILL.md. Two agents on one seed silently clobber each other's tabs, and a re-attaching driver has no way to find the tab it was on before - exactly the shared-browser collision agent-browser filed as #1530.
cuttle_gaps.what_to_build: Add per-connection tab binding in the daemon, where cuttle (unlike agent-browser) can enforce it centrally. New internal/serve/binding.go plus hooks in wsproxy.go: (a) derive a client id per ws connection from an optional ?client=<name> query param on /fingerprint/{seed}/devtools/browser (default: a generated id), persisted per seed under the pool data dir as {seed}/{client}.target with the atomic 0600 fsync+rename write and the corrupt-file-is-an-error rule from tab_binding.rs; (b) observe Target.createTarget responses and Target.attachedToTarget frames on that connection to learn the targetIds it owns, storing {targetId, sanitized url} (strip creds/query/fragment, drop data:/blob: - copy sanitize_url); (c) on reconnect with the same ?client, re-select the bound target: answer the driver's first Target.getTargets with the bound tab first, or, in strict mode (?pin=1 or `cuttle up --pin-tabs`), filter Target.getTargets/targetCreated/attachedToTarget and /json/list so the connection sees only its own targets plus unowned ones, and answer commands aimed at a foreign session with a CDP error carrying a stable code (cuttle mirrors agent-browser's `tab_gone:` shape) instead of letting them land. Reuse the existing frame-rewriting machinery: hideKeepAlive in internal/serve/keepalive.go already strips one targetId from targetCreated/attachedToTarget/targetInfoChanged and from Target.getTargets results - ownership filtering is that function generalized from one id to a set.

cuttle_gaps.risk: Stealth-neutral: all of it is proxy-side frame rewriting, nothing reaches the page or navigator. The real risk is driver compatibility - strict filtering can confuse a driver that expects to enumerate every page (playwright's connectOverCDP adopts all pages in the default context), and a filtered getTargets is a lie a future bug will be blamed on. Keep coherence by shipping the binding non-strict by default (remember and re-select, never hide), and gating hiding/refusal behind an explicit opt-in flag, exactly as agent-browser ships persistence always and --pin-tab opt-in.

cuttle_gaps.gap: No session-inspection verb: an agent cannot ask cuttle what tabs exist, which one `open` will drive, or which seeds are live. `cuttle open` guesses with a heuristic (pickPage in internal/cli/navigate.go: first page target that is not chrome:// and not the VNC viewer URL) and never prints the targetId it chose, so the agent cannot re-address that tab later. The only enumeration path, GET /json/list (internal/serve/http.go handleJSONList), calls getOrLaunch - so listing targets for a seed SPAWNS that seed's Chrome, which also means a typo'd ?fingerprint= creates a whole new identity as a side effect of a read.

cuttle_gaps.gap: The immortal keep-alive tab defends only Target.closeTarget. wsproxy.go's preprocessClient intercepts Target.closeTarget for the keep-alive id, but nothing intercepts Browser.close - one CDP frame from any raw client, puppeteer's browser.close(), or a hand-rolled teardown quits the seed's Chrome outright, taking the window, the tabs, and (on an ephemeral profile) everything not yet snapshotted. The whole keep-alive design intent - 'a driver teardown can never take the browser down with it' - has a one-line hole in it.
cuttle_gaps.what_to_build: Extend the blockContextCreation pattern in internal/serve/wsproxy.go with blockBrowserTeardown: match Browser.close (and Browser.crash / Browser.crashGpuProcess), answer the client with `{"result":{}}` echoing id/sessionId, then close THAT client's websocket normally. This translates 'close the browser' into 'detach this client', which is exactly Playwright's connectOverCDP semantic and agent-browser's explicit rule - so a driver that calls close still sees a clean shutdown while the seed survives. `cuttle down` is unaffected: it terminates via process signals in pool.terminate, not over CDP.

cuttle_gaps.gap: An attached driver cannot tell a browser crash from a clean teardown. proxyCDPWebsocket (internal/serve/wsproxy.go) breaks out of its Chrome-side read loop on ANY error and closes the client with websocket.StatusNormalClosure and an empty reason, whether Chrome crashed, was reaped by --idle-timeout, or the daemon is shutting down. The pool already knows which it was (logChromeExit in pool.go distinguishes signalled/crashed, unexpected clean exit, and pool-initiated), but that knowledge never reaches the client or any status surface, and named seeds are not self-healed at all (superviseDefaultSeed returns immediately for anything but reservedSeed).
cuttle_gaps.what_to_build: On the Chrome-side read error in proxyCDPWebsocket, consult the instance: if cp.process.running() is false, close the client with websocket.StatusInternalError and a reason string ('chrome exited: crash' / 'chrome exited: idle reap' / 'daemon shutting down'). Record a per-seed lastExit{when, reason} on chromePool in pool.go, populated from logChromeExit's existing classification, and expose it in pool.status() so it shows up in GET / and in the `cuttle status` table from the gap above. cuttle_gaps.evidence: vercel-labs/agent-browser cli/src/native/browser.rs:1285 is_connection_alive() (bounded Browser.getVersion probe) and :1303 has_process_exited() (non-blocking child-exit check, reaps the zombie) - the daemon deliberately distinguishes the two; CloakHQ/CloakBrowser-Manager backend/browser_manager.py:427 _on_browser_closed ('Release resources after a browser crash or user-initiated close') logs and reclaims per profile. cuttle: internal/serve/wsproxy.go end-of-loop close, internal/serve/pool.go logChromeExit + superviseDefaultSeed.
cuttle_gaps.risk: None to stealth. Keep the reason strings free of anything site- or credential-derived, since they travel to the driver's transcript.

cuttle_gaps.gap: No handling for renderer-discarded targets. cuttle keeps sessions warm for hours in a memory-capped container and never disables Chrome's tab-discard/Memory-Saver behavior (baseChromeArgs in internal/serve/serve.go carries the three backgrounding switches but nothing about discarding), and neither the daemon nor the CLI probes a target for a live renderer. A discarded tab keeps its CDP target and its /json/list entry, so pickPage will happily hand `cuttle open` a corpse and a driver's Page.enable on it never answers - a hang with no error, which is the single worst failure mode for an agent.

(1) In the new /targets read path (and in pickPage, internal/cli/navigate.go), probe candidates with a bounded Runtime.evaluate('1') in the target's session and mark/skip non-responding ones - copy the shape of agent-browser's renderer_responds/find_live_page_index, including the rule that a CDP *error* still counts as alive. (2) Fold the discard-disabling features into the single --disable-features value that fingerprint.BuildArgs already emits - do NOT append a second --disable-features flag: internal/fingerprint/args.go:218 documents that Chrome takes the last one and BuildArgs dedupes by prefix, so a naive append silently drops the existing NoReferrers,NoCrossOriginReferrers,MinimalReferrers list and changes egress headers.

cuttle_gaps.gap: Attach and inspection share one door, so reading creates identities. Both handleJSONVersion and handleJSONList run getOrLaunch on the raw ?fingerprint= value, meaning any probe - a health check, a curl, an agent enumerating seeds, a typo'd seed name - spawns a full Chrome with its own profile dir, fingerprint, geoip lookup and (with a default proxy configured) egress.
