themes.theme: Knowing when an action landed and when to proceed: actionability gates, stability/settle checks, hit-target verification, navigation and network barriers, retry semantics, and avoiding false "success"
themes.state_of_the_art:
Every mature project in this set treats a click as a five-stage transaction - (a) pre-action checkpoint, (b) state gate, (c) hit-target proof, (d) dispatch, (e) post-action barrier - and refuses to report success unless all five pass. cuttle implements a thin version of (b) and a narrow version of (e), and nothing at all of (a), (c), or the network/navigation half of (e).

PLAYWRIGHT (the canonical implementation, and cuttle's default driver's engine; read from the shipped bundle at ~/.cache/codex-runtimes/codex-primary-runtime/dependencies/node/node_modules/.pnpm/<redacted-email>/node_modules/playwright-core/lib/coreBundle.js, which embeds packages/injected/src/injectedScript.ts and packages/playwright-core/src/server/dom.ts verbatim). The whole contract is written out as the "Life of a pointer action" comment immediately above `setupHitTargetInterceptor` (bundle offset ~996k):
  - `_retryAction` (offset ~1069.6k) loops the entire action with waits [0,20,100,100,500]ms, classifying failures as `error:notvisible` / `error:notinviewport` / `hitTargetDescription` / `missingState` and retrying rather than throwing. `_retryPointerAction` rotates the scroll strategy per retry (undefined -> end/end -> center/center -> start/start) so a target under a sticky header eventually clears it.
  - `Page.performActionPreChecks` (offset ~1177.7k) runs BEFORE every action: `_performWaitForNavigationCheck` blocks while `mainFrame().pendingDocument()` is set (i.e. a navigation is in flight - never click into a doomed document), then `_performLocatorHandlersCheckpoint` fires registered `page.addLocatorHandler` handlers so an interstitial (cookie wall, "session expiring" modal) is dismissed and waited-hidden before the action, then re-checks navigation.
  - Stability is measured in `injected._checkElementIsStable` via `requestAnimationFrame`, not wall-clock sleeps: consecutive rAF samples of `getBoundingClientRect()` must be byte-identical `_stableRafCount` times. Zero fixed latency on a static page.
  - Hit-target proof is two-phase. `expectHitTarget` walks `elementFromPoint` up through `assignedSlot`/shadow hosts and reports a `hitTargetDescription` of the intruder. Then `setupHitTargetInterceptor` installs a capture-phase window listener from the UTILITY (isolated) world that re-runs the hit test on the ACTUAL dispatched `mousedown`/`pointerdown`, and blocks the event if a layout shift moved the target between issuing and handling - "This guarantees no race between issuing the event and handling it in the page."
  - Post-action, `frameManager.waitForSignalsCreatedBy(..., waitAfter, ...)` holds until all navigations triggered by the action commit or cancel, and `stopHitTargetInterception` is raced through `frame.raceAgainstEvaluationStallingEvents` (offset ~1216k), which refuses to evaluate at all when `dialogManager.hasOpenDialogsForPage(page)` - "Open JavaScript dialog prevents evaluation" - or when a document is pending.
  - At the agent layer, `tools/backend/utils.ts waitForCompletion` (bundle ~2912.9k) wraps every CLI/MCP action: record all requests fired during the action, wait 500ms, and if any was a navigation request await `waitForLoadState('load', 10s)`; else await every document/stylesheet/script/xhr/fetch response to finish (5s cap) plus another 500ms. Its `Response._build` (~2974.8k) then appends "Page" (url/title/crashed/console error counts), "Modal state" (open dialogs/file chooser), "Snapshot" and "Events" to EVERY action result. So a playwright-cli agent is told what the page became, not just that a command returned.

CLOAKBROWSER is the closest technical peer to cuttle's problem - a humanized (raw-CDP-input) click layer that must re-implement actionability because it bypasses Playwright's own click. ~/pjv/cloakhq/cloakbrowser/cloakbrowser/human/actionability.py defines a typed error hierarchy (ElementNotAttached/NotVisible/NotStable/NotEnabled/NotEditable/NotReceivingEvents), per-verb check sets (CHECKS_CLICK/HOVER/INPUT/FOCUS/CHECK), a Playwright-matching backoff [100,250,500,1000]ms, and runs all reads through a CDP isolated world (`page._stealth_world`, human/stealth_dom.py) precisely so the checks are invisible to the page - the same stealth constraint cuttle has. Its `check_pointer_events` maps page-space coords into frame-local space before `elementFromPoint` and names the covering tag. Commit e4d4c68 "fix(humanize): re-scroll after the settle wait so clicks land" is the single best piece of evidence in this whole corpus for cuttle's exact failure mode: "An element scrolled into view can be pushed off screen again while we wait for a reflowing page to settle... the click was dispatched outside the viewport and hit nothing, with no error raised." The same commit fixed a second bug: an indeterminate late probe was laundering an already-proven hit-target MISS back into a pass. Issue #329 is the user report.

AGENT-BROWSER is the reference for the proxy/daemon-level concerns cuttle actually owns. ~/pjv/vercel-labs/agent-browser/cli/src/native/interaction.rs:943 `dispatch_mouse_or_dialog` subscribes to the CDP event stream BEFORE sending each of mouseMoved/mousePressed/mouseReleased and races the command against `Page.javascriptDialogOpening` scoped to this click's frame/page session; if the dialog opens between press and release it returns a `PendingRelease` so the button is not left logically down (`dispatch_pending_release`, called from `handle_dialog` in actions.rs:7288 after the dialog resolves). actions.rs:2411 fails page-touching commands FAST with instructions when a confirm/prompt is pending ("would hang until the client read timeout"), and actions.rs:2690 stamps a `warning` field on every response so the agent knows why things are stalling. element.rs:731 `BLOCKER_AT_JS` is the best occlusion probe in the corpus: it descends same-origin iframes rewriting coordinates, walks shadow hosts via `n.host`/`getRootNode().host`, exempts label/control associations, and returns a human-readable `tag#id.class inside section#id` description that becomes the teaching error at element.rs:822 ("...is covered by <div> at its click point, so the input would land on that element instead. Dismiss or interact with the covering element first"). browser.rs:2157 `poll_network_idle` is a correct network-idle: pending-request set, 500ms quiet window, and an explicit recv-timeout branch that starts the idle timer when the subscription began after the page already loaded (the cached-page false-negative).

CLEARCOTE (sdk/python/clearcote/_humanize.py) contributes the "degrade, don't force" rule: its humanized click runs visible -> scroll_into_view -> is_enabled -> two bounding_box samples 50ms apart -> `elementFromPoint` coverage test, and on ANY failure returns to the NATIVE Playwright click "which has its own actionability waits, so this only ever improves - it never regresses". It also documents an engine-side hazard cuttle avoids by construction: `Browser.humanizedClick` answers before the browser process finishes walking the trajectory, so a following `mouse.down()` fired at the stale position and landed on <body> instead of the slider.

CLARK (clarkbrowser/interaction.py) adds only `InteractionPacer`: a min 350ms inter-action interval plus a 900ms SAME-TARGET cooldown, to stop scripts burst-clicking the same element. CLOAKBROWSER-MANAGER contributes nothing on this theme (it is a profile/VNC launcher; its only relevant idea is CDP_START_ATTEMPTS=3 with a verified-ready probe in browser_manager.py:310).

Against that, cuttle (~/Projects/cuttle/internal/serve/humanize.go) has: `awaitStable` (L794) - two `document.elementFromPoint` rect samples 40ms apart in an isolated world of the ROOT frame only, up to 3 retries with [60,150,300]ms backoff, then fail-open and press regardless; and `verifyToggle` (L826) - polls aria-expanded/-pressed/-checked every 35ms for 600ms and re-issues one tight click if the state never moved. wsproxy.go observes no lifecycle, navigation, network or dialog events whatsoever (grep for frameNavigated/javascriptDialogOpening/loadEventFired across internal/ returns only test files).

cuttle_gaps.gap: cuttle has no pre-action navigation barrier. The proxy sees every CDP frame but tracks zero lifecycle state, so an Input.dispatchMouseEvent that arrives while a navigation is in flight is dispatched into the document that is about to be discarded. The settle gate makes this WORSE, not better: awaitStable's probe resolves the old document's elementFromPoint, sees a stable rect (the doomed page is not animating), and green-lights the press.
cuttle_gaps.what_to_build: In internal/serve/wsproxy.go's browser->client loop, passively parse the frames that already flow past (no Page.enable needed when the driver enabled it, which every driver does): Page.frameStartedNavigating / Page.frameRequestedNavigation set a per-session pendingDocument flag; Page.frameNavigated / Page.navigatedWithinDocument / Page.frameStoppedLoading clear it. Hand that state to the humanizer, and have handleMouse's mousePressed branch block on it (bounded, ~5s, fail-open with a log) before running awaitStable. Because cuttle only observes and never enables, there is no risk of surfacing events the driver did not subscribe to.
cuttle_gaps.evidence: playwright-core 1.61.1 bundle, Page.performActionPreChecks -> _performWaitForNavigationCheck (offset ~1177.7k in lib/coreBundle.js, from packages/playwright-core/src/server/page.ts): every action blocks while mainFrame().pendingDocument() is set, logging 'waiting for "<url>" navigation to finish...'. Frame.raceAgainstEvaluationStallingEvents (~1216k) additionally throws 'Frame is currently attempting a navigation' rather than evaluating into a dying document.
cuttle_gaps.risk: None to stealth: it is pure observation of frames already crossing the proxy plus a delay. The only cost is that a driver's click can now be held for up to the barrier timeout; keep it fail-open so a missed frameStoppedLoading can never wedge a session (same discipline as awaitStable today).

cuttle_gaps.gap: cuttle is blind to JavaScript dialogs, and its own settle gate is the thing that pays for it. An open alert/confirm/beforeunload blocks Runtime.evaluate, so every awaitStable probe burns the full 2s queryTimeout before failing open - on a dialog-blocked page each click costs ~2s of dead wait and then presses into a page that cannot receive it. Nothing tells the driver or the agent why. Worse, if a dialog opens from the mousedown handler, cuttle's release (injected fire-and-forget in handleMouse) may never take effect and the button is left logically down, so the next click registers as a drag or double-click.
cuttle_gaps.what_to_build: Track dialog state in wsproxy.go from the passing traffic: Page.javascriptDialogOpening sets a per-session dialog record (type, message, url, defaultPrompt), Page.javascriptDialogClosed clears it. Then (1) humanize.go skips awaitStable/verifyToggle entirely while a dialog is open and forwards Input verbatim - no 2s stalls; (2) on Page.javascriptDialogClosed, if a press was outstanding when the dialog opened, inject the matching mouseReleased; (3) expose it to the agent - add a `GET /pagestate` (or extend `cuttle status`) in internal/serve/http.go returning per-seed {pendingDialog, pendingNavigation} so an agent can see the blocker without a driver verb. Optionally auto-dismiss beforeunload only, and only when the driver has not enabled Page (i.e. cannot possibly be handling it).
cuttle_gaps.evidence: agent-browser cli/src/native/interaction.rs:943 dispatch_mouse_or_dialog races each of the three mouse events against Page.javascriptDialogOpening scoped to this click's sessions, returning PendingRelease when the dialog opened between press and release; actions.rs:7288 dispatches that release once the dialog resolves ('the button is still logically down... otherwise the next click would register as a drag or double-click'). actions.rs:2411 fails page-touching commands fast because a pending confirm/prompt 'blocks the renderer's main thread, so any command that touches the page would hang until the client read timeout'; actions.rs:2690 stamps a `warning` on every response. Playwright: Frame.raceAgainstEvaluationStallingEvents throws 'Open JavaScript dialog prevents evaluation' (bundle ~1216k), and Response._build emits a 'Modal state' section (~2974.8k).
cuttle_gaps.risk: Auto-dismissal is the only stealth-relevant part - a site can detect that a beforeunload was answered instantly. Keep the default to observe-and-report only, and if auto-dismiss is added, delay it by a humanized reaction time (~300-900ms) and never touch confirm/prompt, whose outcome is the agent's decision.

cuttle_gaps.gap: The settle gate proves nothing about WHAT gets clicked. It samples the rect of whatever elementFromPoint returns and presses when the rect stops moving - it never checks that the element under the point is still the same element it was when the gate started, never descends into iframes (probeExpr runs in an isolated world of the ROOT frame only, so a click into any embedded widget/payment/captcha frame gates on the <iframe> box, which is always stable), and never walks shadow hosts. A cookie banner or modal that animates in during the gate's own 40-590ms window, or during the ~50-200ms pre-press dwell + approach that follows, is invisible to it: the gate reports 'settled' and the press lands on the overlay.
cuttle_gaps.what_to_build: Replace probeExpr with an occlusion-aware probe modeled on agent-browser's BLOCKER_AT_JS: descend same-origin iframes rewriting coordinates by each frame's rect + clientLeft/clientTop, walk up through parentNode/host/getRootNode().host, exempt label<->control pairs, and return a stable identity for the hit element (a path/description string plus the aria fields already collected). Compare identity - not just the rect - between the gate's first and last sample AND re-probe once immediately before dispatching mousePressed (after the approach move and the pre-press dwell, which is where an overlay lands today). On an identity change, restart the gate rather than pressing.
cuttle_gaps.evidence: agent-browser cli/src/native/element.rs:731 BLOCKER_AT_JS (iframe descent + shadow-host walk + label exemption + descriptive blocker name) and element.rs:402 check_node_interception, which runs it on every resolved element before dispatch. cloakbrowser cloakbrowser/human/actionability.py check_pointer_events does the same frame-offset mapping and names the covering tag. Playwright injected expectHitTarget walks assignedSlot/parentElementOrShadowHost and returns hitTargetDescription (bundle ~996k).
cuttle_gaps.risk: None - it is the same isolated-world Runtime.evaluate cuttle already issues, just a better expression. It adds no page-observable surface; cost is a slightly larger probe payload.

cuttle_gaps.gap: Post-click verification covers only elements that expose aria-expanded/-pressed/-checked. Plain buttons, submits, links, and every non-ARIA custom control - the large majority of clicks - get zero verification: verifyToggle returns immediately at humanize.go:827 when pressToggleAttr is empty, and the release is forwarded with the driver's ack unchanged. cuttle therefore cannot distinguish 'the click was handled' from 'the click hit a transparent overlay and nothing happened' for most targets.
cuttle_gaps.what_to_build: Before dispatching the press, register a capture-phase listener on window from the SAME isolated world the probe already uses, recording for the first mousedown/pointerdown/click: event.target identity, event.isTrusted, defaultPrevented, and the hit-test result at the event's own clientX/clientY. After the release, read it back (one Runtime.evaluate) and tear it down. Three outcomes: target matches the gate's element -> ack immediately (no aria polling needed, saving the 600ms budget on toggles that already flipped); no event recorded at all -> the click never reached the DOM (blocked page, dialog, browser chrome) -> log and surface it; target mismatched -> the click was stolen, which is exactly when the existing emitTightClick recovery (or a gate restart) should fire. This generalizes verifyToggle from an ARIA special case to every click.
cuttle_gaps.evidence: playwright-core injected setupHitTargetInterceptor (bundle ~996.5k): a capture:true window listener installed from the utility world that re-runs expectHitTarget on the actual dispatched event, with the rationale in the 'Life of a pointer action' comment step 2i: 'we check that hit target at the event point is a descendant of the target element. This guarantees no race between issuing the event and handling it in the page, for example due to layout shift.' It gates on event.isTrusted, exactly like cuttle's events are.
cuttle_gaps.risk: Real but manageable. Playwright's version calls preventDefault/stopImmediatePropagation on a mismatch, which IS page-observable and is a known Playwright tell - do NOT copy the blocking half. An isolated-world listener that only observes is invisible to page JS (the main world cannot enumerate isolated-world listeners; getEventListeners is DevTools-only), so the coherent variant is observe-and-report, with recovery handled by re-clicking rather than by cancelling the page's event.

cuttle_gaps.gap: Stability is sampled on the wall clock, not on frames. awaitStable sleeps a fixed 40ms between the two rect samples, so EVERY press pays >=40ms plus two CDP round-trips even on a completely static page, and a target that moves and returns within that 40ms window reads as stable. The 1px tolerance in probeRectsMatch also passes a slow drift of up to ~25px/s as settled.
cuttle_gaps.what_to_build: Move the stability loop into the probe expression: a single Runtime.evaluate with awaitPromise:true that runs requestAnimationFrame internally, requiring N consecutive frames with a byte-identical getBoundingClientRect before resolving, and resolving immediately on a static page. One round-trip instead of two-plus, no fixed 40ms floor, and no sub-40ms blind spot. Keep the outer retry/backoff and the fail-open deadline (an rAF loop must be bounded - a background/throttled tab does not tick, which is precisely why cuttle already pins Emulation.setFocusEmulationEnabled).
cuttle_gaps.evidence: playwright-core injected _checkElementIsStable (bundle ~1010.6k): requestAnimationFrame loop, exact rect equality, _stableRafCount consecutive frames, with a >15ms guard between samples only when stableRafCount>1. cloakbrowser and clearcote both use the cruder sleep-and-resample form (actionability.py ensure_stable, 100ms; _humanize.py _point_for, 50ms) - Playwright's is strictly better and cuttle can adopt it directly.
cuttle_gaps.risk: None to stealth (same isolated world). Guard against a throttled/hidden frame never ticking rAF by racing an absolute deadline, or the gate turns from a 40ms cost into a hang.

cuttle_gaps.gap: Every failure path is silent. awaitStable fails open after 3 retries and presses anyway; a probe that cannot resolve returns "","" and disables verification; verifyToggle returns silently on any indeterminate read. Nothing is logged with enough specificity to diagnose, and nothing at all reaches the driver or the agent. A click that lands on nothing looks identical to a click that worked - which is the exact silent miss cloakbrowser had to hunt down and fix.
cuttle_gaps.what_to_build: Two cheap pieces. (1) Structured logs in humanize.go for each gate/verify outcome: settled / gave-up-still-moving / point-covered-by-<desc> / no-event-recorded / toggle-never-flipped-reclicked, with the seed and session id, so `cuttle logs` becomes diagnosable. (2) A per-seed ring buffer of the last N such outcomes, exposed on the same `GET /pagestate` endpoint proposed above, so an agent that suspects a no-op click can ask cuttle what it observed instead of guessing from the DOM. Do NOT convert them into CDP errors - failing the driver's command closed would break the fail-open contract - but stop discarding the evidence.
cuttle_gaps.evidence: cloakbrowser commit e4d4c68 'fix(humanize): re-scroll after the settle wait so clicks land': 'the click was dispatched outside the viewport and hit nothing, with no error raised... Measured on a page reflowing 10-25s: silent miss at ~32s before, clean click now.' The same commit fixed a probe timeout laundering a proven miss into 'undetermined' (issue CloakHQ/CloakBrowser#329). agent-browser element.rs:822 intercepted_error shows the teaching-error shape: name the covering element and tell the agent to dismiss it first. cloakbrowser actionability.py defines a whole typed error hierarchy for this.
cuttle_gaps.risk: None. Keep the messages free of site names and page content (the public-repo rule) - log element descriptors and outcome codes, not text content.

cuttle_gaps.gap: The insertText rewrite acks success it has not verified. handleInsertText (humanize.go:582) turns one atomic Input.insertText into up to 80 individual keystrokes over ~10s via fire-and-forget h.inject, then synthesizes okResponse to the driver. Playwright's fill() is exactly this path (injected fill returns 'needsinput' -> keyboard.insertText), so every `playwright-cli fill` on cuttle becomes a 10-second keystroke stream with no check that the field ended up holding the requested value. A React controlled input that re-renders, an autocomplete that steals focus, an input mask, or a maxlength will silently mangle or truncate it - and the driver reports fill() succeeded. The same fabrication applies to mouseMoved and mouseWheel, which are acked with okResponse regardless of what Chrome did.
cuttle_gaps.what_to_build: After the last keystroke and before sending okResponse, run one isolated-world probe reading document.activeElement's value/textContent (and selectionStart) and compare against the requested text. On a match, ack. On a mismatch, repair once - select-all + delete + re-issue the ORIGINAL Input.insertText verbatim (atomic, guaranteed correct, and only reached on a page that already broke the humanized path) - then re-probe and ack. On a second mismatch, ack but log it loudly per the previous gap. This is the mechanical enforcement of the advice cuttle's own SKILL.md already gives agents ('Read state back after you change it', internal/cli/SKILL.md).
cuttle_gaps.evidence: playwright-core dom.ts _fill (bundle ~1083.6k): injected.fill returns 'needsinput' for text inputs and the server then calls page.keyboard.insertText(value) - confirming cuttle's rewrite sits directly under playwright-cli's fill verb. Playwright can skip verification because its insertText is one atomic op; injected.fill DOES verify the branch it sets directly ('if (input.value !== value) throw ... Malformed value'). clearcote _humanize.py hfill takes the other escape hatch - values over 200 chars fall back to native fill 'to keep fill fast/atomic'.
cuttle_gaps.risk: The repair path emits a non-humanized atomic insertText, which is a behavioral tell - but it only fires on a page that already ate the humanized keystrokes, where the alternative is a half-typed field. Gate the repair on an actual mismatch so the common case stays fully humanized, and prefer select-all+retype (still keystrokes) before falling back to insertText.

cuttle_gaps.gap: No same-target re-entrancy guard. verifyToggle can issue a recovery click at the same point ~600ms after the driver's click; an agent that reads the DOM, sees no change yet, and clicks again lands a third press on the same widget. Nothing in cuttle correlates the three, so a menu can be opened, recovered-open, and closed again - and the agent's next snapshot 'proves' the click never worked.
cuttle_gaps.what_to_build: Track (session, rounded x/y, button) -> last dispatch time in the humanizer. If a driver press arrives within a cooldown window (~700-900ms) of a press cuttle already dispatched at effectively the same point, do not swallow it, but delay it until the outstanding verify has completed and re-probe the toggle state first - if the state already flipped since the previous press, log and dispatch normally; if a recovery click is in flight, serialize behind it. This is cheap because handleMouse already keeps lastPressCX/lastPressCY.
cuttle_gaps.evidence: clark-browser clarkbrowser/interaction.py InteractionPacer: _DEFAULT_SAME_TARGET_COOLDOWN_MS = 900 alongside a 350ms global min interval, existing specifically so 'scripts do not burst-click' the same target. Playwright reaches the same place from the other side - _retryAction serializes retries of one action and never lets two dispatches for the same logical click overlap.
cuttle_gaps.risk: A cooldown that is too aggressive would throttle legitimate double-clicks; scope it to single-click presses (clickCount==1) and never to a driver's explicit dblclick, which arrives as clickCount 2.

cuttle_gaps.gap: No post-action network/quiescence signal, and no way for an agent to ask for one. cuttle acks the release the moment its verify window closes; whether the click kicked off a navigation or a burst of XHR is unknown to the proxy and unknowable to the agent from cuttle's side. Agents on playwright-cli get this from Playwright's own waitForCompletion, but agent-browser and browser-use users - both first-class in cuttle's SKILL.md - do not, and cuttle's guidance ('Never sleep; wait for a condition') hands them no cuttle-side condition to wait on.
cuttle_gaps.what_to_build: Extend the same passive event tap from gap 1 to Network.requestWillBeSent / loadingFinished / loadingFailed (again only observing what the driver already enabled - most drivers enable Network) and maintain a per-session in-flight count plus a last-quiet timestamp. Surface it on GET /pagestate as {inflight, quietForMs, lastNavigationAt, pendingDialog}, and document the poll-until-quiet pattern in internal/cli/SKILL.md so any driver can use it. Do not block the driver's ack on it - report it, because cuttle cannot know which requests the agent's next step actually depends on.
cuttle_gaps.evidence: playwright-core tools/backend/utils.ts waitForCompletion (bundle ~2912.9k): record requests during the action, wait 500ms, branch on whether a navigation request was made (waitForLoadState('load'), 10s) versus awaiting document/stylesheet/script/xhr/fetch responses (5s cap) plus 500ms. agent-browser browser.rs:2157 poll_network_idle: pending-request set, 500ms quiet window, plus an explicit recv-timeout branch that starts the idle timer when the subscription began after load ('prevents false-positive idle detection when the subscription starts after the page has already loaded, e.g. cached pages') - with unit tests for exactly that at browser.rs:2815.
cuttle_gaps.risk: None to stealth (pure observation). The real risk is scope creep against KISS - resist adding a blocking `wait` verb to cuttle: the drivers own waiting. Ship it as read-only state plus one paragraph of SKILL.md guidance.

cuttle_gaps.gap: No pre-action interstitial checkpoint. When a cookie wall, 'session expiring' modal, or Cloudflare interstitial appears mid-flow, cuttle's gate sees a perfectly stable overlay under the point and clicks it. The agent then re-reads a DOM that never changed and loops. This is the only item where the upstream answer (Playwright locator handlers) does not port cleanly, because cuttle has no selectors.
cuttle_gaps.what_to_build: Do not build a handler registry. The cuttle-shaped version is the occlusion probe from gap 3 plus reporting from gap 6: when the press point resolves to an element that is NOT the element the gate first saw, and the intruder is a full-viewport or fixed-position node, log/report 'point covered by <desc>' rather than pressing. The agent - which does have selectors - dismisses it. If a mechanism is ever wanted, the honest minimal one is a per-seed list of CSS selectors in the profile store that the proxy checks in the isolated world before a press and clicks first; treat that as a later, separately justified feature.
cuttle_gaps.evidence: playwright-core page.ts _performLocatorHandlersCheckpoint (bundle ~1178k) runs registered addLocatorHandler handlers before EVERY action and, unless noWaitAfter, waits for the handler's selector to become hidden before letting the action through. agent-browser reaches the same outcome without a registry by failing closed with a teaching error naming the blocker (element.rs:822).
cuttle_gaps.risk: A cuttle-side auto-dismiss registry would be a KISS/YAGNI violation and a stealth liability (a proxy clicking consent buttons the agent never asked for, at machine timing, on pages the user did not authorize writes to). Keep cuttle in the detect-and-report role; dismissal stays an explicit agent action.

themes.theme: Behavioral humanization and what it costs: trajectory models, keystroke dynamics, scroll profiles, per-action tunability vs global daemon flag, and measured evidence of what detectors actually score.
themes.state_of_the_art:
Three genuinely different architectures exist across these repos, and cuttle sits in the weakest tier of the one that matters most (the motion model), while being alone in the strongest tier of another (driver-agnostic CDP-proxy placement).

**1. clearcote-browser is the state of the art on the motion model itself, and it is the only project that MEASURES it.**

`~/pjv/clearcotelabs/clearcote-browser/sdk/node/src/motion.ts` (377 lines, mirrored byte-for-behavior in `sdk/python/clearcote/_motionscore.py` / `_motion`) is a pure, I/O-free planner. Its stated model, from the file header:
- **Minimum-jerk sum-of-submovements** (Meyer's optimized-submovement model), not a single Bezier. `planMove()` builds a primary ballistic submovement landing at `primaryFrac` (0.84-0.94 of the gap) with a gaussian over/undershoot, then 1-2 corrective submovements each closing 55-80% of the residual, with a 40-120 ms "motor re-planning gap" between them. Each submovement is eased with `minJerk(t) = 10t^3 - 15t^4 + 6t^5` and time-allocated 78% primary / 22% corrections. The header states the reason explicitly: *"A single bezier peaks at the wrong place and has exactly one submovement - a structural tell."*
- **Colored noise**, not white: Ornstein-Uhlenbeck drift (`driftTau` 60-160 ms) + a band-limited **8-12 Hz physiological tremor** with continuous absolute-clock phase across submovements, amplitude "breathing", and a detuned (0.93x) y-axis so it is not a fixed tone in exact quadrature; plus an AR(1) sub-pixel jitter (`jit.x = 0.7*jit.x + gauss*0.22`). Comment: *"white noise adds a fresh speed reversal every sample, manufacturing spurious submovements and a flat noise spectrum."*
- **Per-identity motor persona seeded from the fingerprint seed** (`makePersona(seed)` in motion.ts, threaded from `launch()` via `HumanizeOptions.seed`): deviceHz 110-155, tremorHz 8-12, tremorAmp, driftAmp/tau, fittsA 90-150 ms, fittsB 120-190 ms/bit, primaryFrac, overshoot, maxCorrections, handedness `approachBias`, grab 130-360 ms, release 90-230 ms, clickHold 60-150 ms, keyDwell 45-120 ms. Same seed => same motor signature; different seeds => unlinkable. Their patch doc calls fixed constants out by name as a defect: *"Fixed distribution profilable over long sessions - seeded per-eTLD+1"* (`docs/PATCHES.md:158`).
- **Endpoint dwells for drags**: `dragDwell()` returns grab (down -> first movement) and release (last movement -> up) windows, described as *"the two worst slider tells: real ~130-360 ms grab / ~90-230 ms release vs a scripted few ms."*
- **Ambient pre-goal pointer entropy**: `planAmbient(from, viewport, persona, ms)` emits idle drift plus non-goal excursions inside a central band (12-88% x, 14-80% y), *"so a behavioral collector sees non-zero pointer entropy BEFORE the first goal action (the single biggest reason a challenge/slider is shown to headless automation)."* It is exposed as opt-in `page.ambientMotion(ms)` and `page._clearcoteAutoAmbient`, deliberately defaulted OFF because it interleaves with caller-driven input (`sdk/node/src/humanize.ts:~290`).
- **A detector emulator with a score and named flags**: `sdk/node/src/motionscore.ts` (241 lines) extracts `peakVelFrac`, `velSkew`, `submovements`, `straightness`, `dtUniform` (fraction of inter-sample dt within +/-20% of the median - a real device stream has a cadence MODE; `rand(a,b)` is flat), `jitterAutocorr` (lag-1 on the residual), `powerLawR` (diagnostic only - they explicitly refuse to impose the 2/3 power law during generation because it governs continuous drawing, not discrete reaches), and drag `grabMs`/`releaseMs`. `scoreMotion()` penalizes: peakVelFrac > 0.48 (-0.12, "too-symmetric"), velSkew < 0.1 (-0.12), submovements < 1 (-0.2), submovements > 4 (-0.12), dtUniform (-0.15), jitterAutocorr < 0.1 (-0.1), straightness > 0.9995 (-0.08), grabMs < 60 / releaseMs < 40 (-0.2 each).
- **It is wired into CI.** `sdk/node/test/motion.test.ts` contains `oldGlide()` - a faithful reproduction of their *previous* single-bezier + smoothstep + `rand(7,20)` dt + white-gauss-jitter glide - and asserts `newAvg > oldAvg` and `newAvg > 0.75`, plus per-feature assertions (submovements >= 1 and < 3.5, velSkew > 0.1, jitterAutocorr > 0.1, `dtUniform` never fires, Fitts: a small target takes longer than a large one at equal distance).

I ported cuttle's `planMouseMove` (internal/serve/humanize.go:170-226) verbatim into TypeScript and ran it through clearcote's own scorer, 200 runs, identical geometry (200,300)->(720,470), mulberry32-seeded:

```
cuttle avg score: 0.645   clearcote avg score: 0.953
cuttle mean features: submovements 0.38, velSkew -0.31, jitterAutocorr 0.89,
                      peakVelFrac 0.480, dtUniform rate 0.26, durationMs 632
cuttle flags fired (of 200): velocity-symmetric 187, no-corrective-submovement 141,
                             peak-velocity-too-symmetric 101, uniform-dt-cadence 52,
                             perfectly-straight-path 5
```
(script: `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-tenequm-Projects-cuttle/S01/scratchpad/score.ts`)

cuttle's correlated tremor genuinely works (jitterAutocorr 0.89, better than the 0.1 floor - this is the one axis where cuttle already beats naive humanizers, and it should be kept). Everything else fails: cuttle's `easeInOut(p, skew)` smoothstep with skew 0.85-1.15 puts peak velocity at ~0.48 and produces a *negatively* skewed (symmetric-to-left-tailed) velocity profile, and its only source of a corrective submovement is the 14% `overshootProb` - so 70% of cuttle moves have zero corrections. cuttle IS the `oldGlide()` baseline clearcote wrote its new model to beat.

**2. clearcote also solved the CDP-marker and cost problem in C++, which is a level cuttle can reach because it ships its own Chromium.** `patches/130-humanized-input.patch` (3791 lines) and `patches/200-agent-and-humanized-input.patch` add browser-level CDP methods `Browser.humanizedClick` / `humanizedClickSelector`, implemented as a `HumanizedClickRunner` state machine driven by `base::OneShotTimer` in the browser process, constructing `WebMouseEvent` with **kNoModifiers (no `blink::WebInputEvent::kFromDebugger`)** and routing via `RenderWidgetHostInputEventRouter::RouteMouseEvent`. Their doc (`docs/PATCHES.md:156-159`) rates this P1 and rates the CDP `Input.dispatchMouseEvent` humanizer (cuttle's exact placement) as a *fallback* precisely because *"This path still carries kFromDebugger via CreateWebMouseEvent."* A separate P2 item removes `modifiers |= kFromDebugger` from `synthetic_mouse_driver.cc` (lines 58, 92, 124) and `synthetic_smooth_move_gesture.cc:309`. The cost win is structural: the browser walks the trajectory itself and answers the CDP command immediately, so the driver's connection is never blocked - though the SDK documents the sharp edge that follows (`humanize.ts:~150`): the engine answers before the path finishes and *overruns* its reported duration, so a following `mouse.down()` fired at a stale position (measured: a move to (110,58) pressed at (981,629) on `<body>`); their fix is to sleep the duration and re-pin with a native move before every press, and to keep all held-button drags on the native path entirely (measured: 672 of 829 held moves reported `MouseEvent.buttons === 0` when routed through the engine, so a range slider never moved).

**3. CloakBrowser is the state of the art on tunability and per-element awareness, at the SDK layer.** `cloakbrowser/human/config.py` is a 40-field `HumanConfig` dataclass with two shipped presets (`default`, `careful`) and, critically, `merge_config(base, overrides)` so *every* wrapped call takes `human_config={...}`: `page.type(sel, text, human_config={"typing_delay": 30})`. The CHANGELOG lists "Per-call `human_config` - override humanize settings on individual method calls" as a shipped feature. Because it wraps Playwright's Locator/ElementHandle API rather than CDP, it knows the element: `click_target(box, is_input, cfg)` in `human/mouse.py` picks a landing point at `x_frac in (0.05, 0.30)` for text inputs (people click near the start of a field) vs `(0.35, 0.65)` for buttons, with separate aim-delay and hold windows per kind (`click_aim_delay_input` 60-140 vs `click_aim_delay_button` 80-200; `click_hold_input` 40-100 vs `click_hold_button` 60-150). Its scroll (`human/scroll.py`) is target-aware: it moves the cursor into a random central scroll area first, scrolls under accelerate -> cruise -> decelerate with `_smooth_wheel()` breaking each logical scroll into 20-40 px sub-notches at 8-20 ms, re-checks element visibility every 3 steps, stops at a `scroll_target_zone` of (0.20, 0.80) of the viewport, and applies a 10% chance of overshoot followed by 1-2 corrections and a 300-600 ms settle. It also has `idle_between_actions` / `idle_drift_px` for micro-drift between actions (on in the `careful` preset). Its README is blunt about the mechanism cuttle also fixed: *"Use `page.type()` instead of `page.fill()` - `fill()` sets values directly without keyboard events, which reCAPTCHA's behavioral analysis flags."* Their claimed evidence: deviceandbrowserinfo.com behavioral detection 24/24 signals, 6 true bot flags -> 0, and a server-verified 0.9 reCAPTCHA v3 score with `humanize=True`.

**4. clark-browser contributes the inter-action layer nobody else has.** `clarkbrowser/interaction.py` is a small `InteractionPacer`/`AsyncInteractionPacer`: `min_interval_ms=350` between any two actions, `jitter_ms=200` added only when a wait is already needed, and `same_target_cooldown_ms=900` keyed on `f"click:{selector}"` so a retry loop cannot burst-click one element. Seeded RNG, injectable clock. This models the *gap between* actions, which is a separate detector feature from the motion within one.

**5. The drivers themselves do nothing.** microsoft/playwright-cli is a skill/test wrapper with no humanization surface at all. vercel-labs/agent-browser has exactly one knob: an optional `delay` (ms) forwarded to `interaction::type_text` (`cli/src/native/actions.rs:5165`), no mouse model; its documented default action timeout is 25 s (`skill-data/core/SKILL.md:192`). This confirms cuttle's architectural bet - humanizing at the CDP-proxy layer is the only place it can happen for these drivers, and cuttle is the only project here that does it driver-agnostically. That bet is right; the model running inside it is what is behind.
