Straight verbatim-forwarding above a very large ceiling should remain as the last-resort backstop.

cuttle_gaps.gap: Three CDP input surfaces bypass the humanizer entirely. `handleClientFrame` switches on exactly `Input.dispatchMouseEvent`, `Input.dispatchKeyEvent` and `Input.insertText` (internal/serve/humanize.go, the switch after `decodeCDP`); everything else returns false and is forwarded untouched and instantaneous. That leaves `Input.dispatchTouchEvent` (any mobile-emulation flow - agent-browser ships a `mobile` tools profile), `Input.dispatchDragEvent` (playwright-core's HTML5 drag-and-drop path when drag interception is on), and `Input.synthesizeScrollGesture` / `Input.synthesizePinchGesture` (touch-style scrolling) as instant, teleporting input arriving in the middle of an otherwise carefully humanized session - which is a worse signal than uniformly instant input, because the contrast is itself informative.
cuttle_gaps.what_to_build: Extend the switch. `Input.dispatchTouchEvent` is the closest analogue to the existing mouse path - a touchStart/touchMove/touchEnd sequence takes the same trajectory planner with a touch-appropriate persona (larger tremor, no sub-pixel precision) and the same paced dispatch. For `Input.dispatchDragEvent` the honest minimum is to pace the dragEnter/dragOver stream and add the grab/release dwells from gap 8 rather than model it fully. For `synthesizeScrollGesture` the cheapest correct move is to decompose it the way `planScroll` already decomposes a wheel. If any of these is genuinely unreachable for cuttle's drivers, the KISS answer is to log a one-line warning when an unhandled `Input.*` method crosses the proxy on a humanize-enabled session, so the blind spot is visible rather than silent - and build nothing else.
cuttle_gaps.evidence: Verifiable directly from cuttle's switch in internal/serve/humanize.go (`case methodMouse / methodKey / methodInsertText / default: return false`). clearcote treats the synthetic-gesture path as a first-class surface needing its own patch (docs/PATCHES.md:159, `humanize-synthetic-gesture-unmark`, targeting synthetic_mouse_driver.cc and synthetic_smooth_move_gesture.cc). CloakBrowser's drag coverage is visible in tests/test_human_visual.py, which instruments `drag`, `dragover` and `dragend` alongside mousemove precisely because the drag path is distinct.
cuttle_gaps.risk: Low stealth risk, real YAGNI risk: if no cuttle driver ever emits touch or drag events, all three handlers are dead code that the non-negotiables say to delete rather than write. Establish which methods actually appear in a real session first - the one-line warning IS that instrumentation, and shipping only the warning is a defensible complete answer to this gap.

cuttle_gaps.gap: Every click lands on the exact pixel the driver named, and the Fitts target width is a guessed constant. cuttle presses at the driver's coordinate with an explicit "NO off-centre re-aim" (the comment in `handleMouse` case "mousePressed" records that a previous off-centre pick fired a stray micro-move between approach and press and broke Material/CDK selects). The cost is that `planMouseMove` uses `fittsW = 18.0` with the comment "The Input layer carries no element size" - which is no longer true at press time: `awaitStable` runs BEFORE the approach move and its `probeExpr` already returns `{x, y, w, h}` from `getBoundingClientRect()`. So cuttle pays a round-trip for the element rect and then throws away the width and the landing distribution, meaning every click lands dead on one repeatable point with a Fitts duration computed from a fiction.
cuttle_gaps.what_to_build: Reuse the rect cuttle already fetches. (1) Feed the probe's real `w`/`h` into the Fitts index in place of the `fittsW` constant, so movement time actually scales with target size - the one property clearcote's Fitts test asserts and the property that makes the timing distribution defensible across short-hop-big-target and long-hop-small-target. (2) For the landing point, avoid reintroducing the stray micro-move by applying the offset at the MOVE, not the press: run the probe on `mouseMoved` at the destination, pick a 2D-gaussian point inside the rect (sigma ~0.16 of width/height, clamped 2 px inside the edges, biased ~12% back toward the approach direction - people undershoot toward where the cursor came from), and make that the single trajectory endpoint. The press then arrives at the driver's coordinate and reuses `lastClickX/lastClickY`, which cuttle's release path already does - so the click stays one coherent gesture with no second move, which is exactly the invariant the old code violated.
cuttle_gaps.evidence: ~/pjv/clearcotelabs/clearcote-browser/sdk/node/src/motion.ts - `clickPoint(box, from, p, rng)`: gaussian at 0.16 of box width/height around center, 12% approach-side undershoot bias, clamped 2 px inside, with a center fallback for boxes under 4 px. `PlanOpts.targetW` feeds the Fitts index and is asserted in sdk/node/test/motion.test.ts:88-96 (`dur(8) > dur(120)`). CloakBrowser's element-aware version is `click_target(box, is_input, cfg)` in cloakbrowser/human/mouse.py - `click_input_x_range = (0.05, 0.30)` for text inputs vs `rand(0.35, 0.65)` for buttons, with separate aim/hold windows per element kind (config.py `click_aim_delay_input` vs `click_aim_delay_button`).
cuttle_gaps.risk: This is the one that already bit cuttle once, and the scar tissue in the code is a warning worth heeding. Part (1) - using the real width for Fitts - is safe and independent; ship it alone. Part (2) moves the probe from press-time to move-time, adding a round-trip per move (bounded by the existing 2 s `queryTimeout`, fail-open) and changing where the offset is applied; it must not reintroduce a second dispatch between approach and press, and it needs regression coverage against the Material/CDK select case the original comment names. If that coverage does not exist, ship (1) and leave (2).

cuttle_gaps.gap: No inter-action pacing. cuttle humanizes WITHIN an action but models nothing BETWEEN actions: a driver retry loop can fire the same click at the same coordinate five times in ~2.5 s with nothing but the intrinsic ~0.5 s action cost separating them, and there is no reading pause, no post-navigation settle, and no cooldown for a repeated target. The gap distribution between actions is a distinct feature from the motion within one, and a burst of identical clicks on one point is a cheap, obvious pattern.
cuttle_gaps.what_to_build: Add a small pacer to the humanizer, keyed on `sid` plus a quantized coordinate bucket: enforce a persona-drawn minimum interval between consecutive humanized actions, add jitter ONLY when a wait is already owed (so it does not tax an already-slow sequence), and apply a longer cooldown when the same bucket is targeted twice in a row. Gate it on the humanize tier so `fast` skips it. Roughly 40 lines using the existing `h.sleep` and `h.mu`, no new file - the persona from gap 4 supplies the numbers.
cuttle_gaps.evidence: ~/pjv/clark-labs-inc/clark-browser/clarkbrowser/interaction.py - `InteractionPacer` / `AsyncInteractionPacer` with `_DEFAULT_MIN_INTERVAL_MS = 350`, `_DEFAULT_JITTER_MS = 200`, `_DEFAULT_SAME_TARGET_COOLDOWN_MS = 900`, keyed as `f"click:{selector}"`, and the deliberate design note "adds bounded jitter only when a wait is already needed". CloakBrowser's variant is inter-action idle drift rather than a pure wait: `idle_between_actions` / `idle_between_duration (0.3, 0.8)` (on in the `careful` preset) plus `human_idle()` in cloakbrowser/human/mouse.py, and `field_switch_delay (800, 1500)` for moving between form fields.
cuttle_gaps.risk: Directly adds latency on top of an already-slow path, so it must ride the tier control from gap 3 rather than being unconditional - otherwise it makes the exact complaint that motivated the tier worse. There is also a real overlap question with the settle gate and `verifyToggle`, which already impose sub-second waits around clicks; measure the actual inter-action gap distribution a cuttle session produces today before adding more waiting, because the intrinsic action cost may already put cuttle inside the human envelope, in which case the correct action is to build nothing.

themes.theme: Agent-facing API shape: verb design, structured vs prose output, error quality and recovery data, self-documenting skill files, token cost, and MCP-vs-CLI as the agent interface
themes.state_of_the_art:
Four distinct design stances are visible across these repos, and cuttle sits closest to the weakest one on every axis except prose quality.

**1. Structured output is a first-class, dual-rendered concern (playwright-cli).** `packages/playwright-core/src/tools/cli-client/output.ts` (microsoft/playwright, path `packages/playwright-core/src/tools/cli-client/`, mirrored into the `@playwright/cli` npm package) defines a single `interface Output` with `TextOutput` and `JsonOutput` implementations selected by the global `--json` flag. Critically, EVERY error is a named method on that interface (`errorUnknownCommand`, `errorDetachNotAttached`, `errorBrowserNotOpenForTool`, `errorAttachNoTarget`, `errorAttachConflict`, `errorInstallGlobalRequiresSkills`), so an error cannot be added without deciding both its human rendering and its `{isError: true, error}` JSON rendering, and each carries the remedy inline (`errorBrowserNotOpenForTool` prints the literal `playwright-cli -s=<session> open [params]` line to run next). Success payloads are typed too (`ListedBrowser`, `ListData`), and `renderChannelSession()` emits per-target ready-to-paste attach commands.

**2. Errors carry machine codes plus the data needed to recover (agent-browser).** `cli/src/native/browser.rs:416` defines `TAB_GONE_PREFIX`, and `cli/src/native/actions.rs:11448` stamps `resp["code"] = json!("tab_gone")` alongside `data.targetId` and a sanitized `data.lastUrl` so an agent can re-bind rather than guess. `cli/src/native/element.rs:824` is the model for actionability errors: "Element '{}' is covered by <{}> at its click point, so the input would land on that element instead. Dismiss or interact with the covering element first (it is often a dialog, banner, or sticky header)." - it names the blocker element AND prescribes the fix. State-mutating results carry advisory flags rather than failing silently: `cli/src/native/browser.rs:1642-1647` sets `result["revived"] = true` when Chrome's Memory Saver discarded and reloaded a tab, and `result["dialogBlocked"] = true` when the target tab's renderer is paused by a dialog.

**3. Native dialogs are modelled explicitly, not ignored (agent-browser).** `cli/src/native/actions.rs:1700-1727` subscribes to `Page.javascriptDialogOpening`/`javascriptDialogClosed` on the daemon's CDP event loop and holds a `PendingDialog{dialog_type, message, url, default_prompt, session_id}`. `alert` and `beforeunload` are auto-handled by a background `dialog_handler_task` (opt out with `--no-auto-dialog`, `cli/src/flags.rs:1001`) and deliberately not tracked. For `confirm`/`prompt`, `actions.rs:2411-2450` fails the next page-touching command FAST with `A JavaScript {type} dialog is blocking the page: "{message}". Resolve it with \`dialog accept\` or \`dialog dismiss\`, then retry \`{action}\`.` - with an explicit allowlist of commands that stay usable while blocked (`dialog`, `screenshot`, `url`, `title`, `tab_list/new/switch/close`), because switching tabs is how an agent escapes. Two second-order details matter: `actions.rs:3893` skips the periodic state autosave while a dialog is pending, with the comment "A JS dialog blocks the renderer's main thread, so the storage-collection evaluate would hang until its CDP timeout"; and `actions.rs:7295` releases a `pending_pointer_release` after `Page.handleJavaScriptDialog`, because a mousedown that opened the dialog left the button logically down and the next click would register as a drag or double-click.

**4. Skills are served by the binary and version-locked, not copy-pasted (both CLIs).** agent-browser splits `skills/agent-browser/SKILL.md` (a 51-line discovery stub with `hidden: true` frontmatter, existing only for `npx skills add`, whose entire body says "This file is a discovery stub, not the usage guide... load the actual workflow content from the CLI") from `skill-data/core/SKILL.md` (516 lines) plus ten `skill-data/core/references/*.md` and three `skill-data/core/templates/*.sh`. `cli/src/skills.rs` resolves them from the package root and serves `skills list`, `skills get core`, `skills get core --full`, `skills get electron|slack|dogfood|derive-client|vercel-sandbox|agentcore`. playwright-cli installs its skill INTO the repo (`playwright-cli install --skills` -> `.claude/skills/playwright-cli/`, `--skills=agents` -> `.agents/skills/`) and then `skillCheck.js` byte-compares the installed copy against the bundled one on every non-`install` invocation, printing a boxed "The playwright-cli skill at '...' does not match the tool version. Run `playwright-cli install --skills`". Its `skills/playwright-cli/SKILL.md` is 420 lines with nine `references/*.md` linked at the bottom under "Specific tasks".

**5. Token cost is engineered, not hoped for.** playwright-cli's default snapshot output is a FILE REFERENCE, not content: `### Snapshot\n[Snapshot](.playwright-cli/page-2026-02-14T19-22-42-679Z.yml)` (the `.playwright-cli` dir comes from `outputDir()` in `packages/playwright-core/src/tools/backend/context.ts`, which switches base name on `config.skillMode`). Narrowing verbs exist so a full dump is rarely needed: `find "Sign in"` / `find --regex` returns matching nodes with 3 lines of context like `grep -C`, `snapshot --depth=4`, `snapshot e34`, and `open --mobile` is recommended explicitly because "mobile pages are usually lighter, so snapshots are smaller and cheaper." agent-browser caps output globally with `--max-output <chars>` / `AGENT_BROWSER_MAX_OUTPUT` and appends `[truncated: showing {} of {} chars. Use --max-output to adjust]` (`cli/src/output.rs:50`). clearcote's MCP does the same at the tool boundary: `_cap(result, {"text": 20000, "markdown": 40000})` sets a sibling `{field}_truncated: true` flag (`mcp/clearcote_mcp/server.py`).

**6. Secrets are handled by the tool, not by agent discipline.** `packages/playwright-core/src/tools/backend/context.ts:353-370`: `lookupSecret(name)` substitutes the real value into the action while codegen emits a `secretCode(...)` reference, and `redactSecrets(text)` does `text.replaceAll(secretValue, '<secret>NAME</secret>')` over every tool response (`backend/response.ts:220`), every file the tool writes (`response.ts:119`), and the session log artifact (`backend/logFile.ts:94`). Loaded from `--secrets <dotenv>` or `PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_SECRETS_FILE` (`tools/mcp/config.ts:444`). CloakBrowser-Manager solves the same problem physically for a VNC farm: `POST /api/profiles/{profile_id}/clipboard` (`backend/main.py:641`) spawns `xclip -selection clipboard` on the profile's `DISPLAY` so a value can be pasted into the browser without ever being typed or echoed, and `GET /api/profiles/{profile_id}/clipboard` (`main.py:677`) reads it back via a Playwright-injected `window.__clipboardText` because Chrome under KasmVNC never writes to the X11 clipboard.

**7. A self-diagnosis verb exists, and it is structured.** agent-browser ships `cli/src/doctor/` behind `doctor [--json] [--fix] [--offline] [--quick] [--webgpu]`, documented as the FIRST thing to run on any unexpected failure, auto-cleaning stale socket/pid/version sidecars, gating destructive repairs behind `--fix`, and exiting 0/1. CloakBrowser has `python -m cloakbrowser info|doctor` with a hard-won detail in `cloakbrowser/__main__.py:75-90`: on Windows it appends `--no-startup-window` to the `--version` probe because Chromium there ignores `--version` and launches a browser instead, so a healthy install times out and looks broken.

**8. MCP vs CLI is an explicit parity contract where both exist.** agent-browser's `AGENTS.md` makes it a rule: "When adding or changing any CLI command, flag, behavior, output, environment variable, or parser semantics, update the MCP server in `cli/src/mcp.rs` in the same change... Add or update tests that prove the CLI and MCP surfaces remain aligned." Its MCP server is profile-paginated (`--tools core,network,state,debug,tabs,react,mobile,all`) so tool-discovery context stays small, and every typed tool takes an `extraArgs` escape hatch for exact CLI parity. clearcote's MCP (`mcp/clearcote_mcp/server.py`) is the minimal-surface counterexample and is worth copying at the boundary level even if you never ship MCP: a `_safe` decorator gives every tool a wall-clock timeout (`CLEARCOTE_MCP_TOOL_TIMEOUT`, default 90s) and returns `{"status": "error", "error": "..."}` instead of throwing; `ToolAnnotations(readOnlyHint=..., openWorldHint=...)` classifies each tool; and `get_cdp_endpoint` returns the raw endpoint alongside a `connect` dict of ready-to-paste snippets for playwright-python, playwright-node, puppeteer, and browser-use - the structured form of what cuttle's briefing prints as text. `get_egress_info` returns the egress IP AND the active persona together so an agent can verify identity coherence.

Against all of that, cuttle today: zero `--json` anywhere (verified by reading every `Use:`/`RunE` in `internal/cli/commands.go`); errors are `fmt.Errorf` strings with no code (`internal/cli/commands.go:75,581,583,732,781,976,1008,1031`) - the prose remedies are genuinely good ("run `cuttle status` to triage, then `cuttle down` and retry") but nothing is parseable and `runStatus` prints a human block then returns a bare `errUnhealthy` sentinel; a 489-line monolithic `internal/cli/SKILL.md` served all-or-nothing by `cuttle skill` (`internal/cli/skill.go`, 31 lines) with no install path, no drift check, no topic addressing, and an explicit instruction not to truncate it; no `doctor`; no screenshot verb; no dialog awareness anywhere in `internal/serve/`; and a structured status payload that already exists at `GET /` (`chromePool.status()` in `internal/serve/pool.go` returns per-seed pid/port/seed/connections/timezone/locale/proxy) but is undocumented in SKILL.md and unreachable from the CLI. The one place cuttle is genuinely ahead is `internal/cli/drivers.go` - the driver registry that refuses to bake in other tools' docs and instead prints each driver's own `docs` command, so instructions can never go stale. That idea is better than what any of the others do for cross-tool docs.

cuttle_gaps.gap: cuttle is blind to native JavaScript dialogs, and its humanizer actively makes the blindness worse. Nothing in internal/serve/ references Page.javascriptDialogOpening, Page.javascriptDialogClosed, or Page.handleJavaScriptDialog. When a beforeunload/confirm/alert is open the renderer's main thread is paused, so: (a) humanize.go's pre-click settle gate awaitStable() calls h.query() -> Runtime.evaluate, which hangs to its timeout and then FAILS OPEN (internal/serve/humanize.go:782-814, comment: 'ANY doubt ... returns immediately, so a click is never blocked'), pressing into a frozen page; (b) verifyToggle() then polls the same paused renderer for the whole togglePollBudget and re-issues one more tight click (humanize.go:826-850); (c) if the mousePressed itself opened the dialog, cuttle's split press/release (handleMouse 'mousePressed' forwards, then sleeps h.clickHold() before 'mouseReleased', humanize.go:425-475) strands the button logically DOWN, so the next click reads as a drag or double-click; (d) extractSeedState()'s checkpoint evaluate hangs to captureTimeout and the snapshot is skipped (internal/serve/supervise.go:116-140). The agent sees only slow, silently-failing clicks - exactly the reported pain #4.
cuttle_gaps.what_to_build: In internal/serve/wsproxy.go, extend the existing pinPage(sid) hook (which already fires per Target.attachedToTarget and for direct /devtools/page/ dials) to sendInjected 'Page.enable' on each attached page session. Add a per-connection pendingDialog map[sessionID]dialogInfo{type,message,url,defaultPrompt} fed by prefiltering inbound frames for the byte string "javascriptDialog" (same bytes.Contains-then-decode pattern as attachedToTargetBytes). Then: (1) auto-dismiss beforeunload and alert by injecting Page.handleJavaScriptDialog{accept:true} and NOT recording them as pending - agent-browser's default, with a `cuttle up --no-auto-dialog` daemon flag to opt out; (2) for confirm/prompt, record pending and let the frame through to the driver unchanged, but gate the humanizer: add `if h.dialogPending(sid) { return false }` at the top of handleClientFrame so Input.* forwards raw instead of running a settle gate and toggle verify against a paused renderer; (3) track a pendingPointerRelease when a mousePressed is followed by a dialog and dispatch the release immediately after any Page.handleJavaScriptDialog, mirroring cli/src/native/actions.rs:7290-7300; (4) add `GET /dialogs?fingerprint=<seed>` returning `{"dialogs":[{"targetId":..,"type":"beforeunload","message":..,"url":..}]}` and a `cuttle dialogs [accept|dismiss [text]]` verb over it, mirroring how `cuttle downloads` wraps GET /downloads; (5) skip the supervisor checkpoint for a seed with a pending dialog (guard in supervise.go doCapture, copying actions.rs:3893's rationale verbatim).
cuttle_gaps.evidence: vercel-labs/agent-browser: cli/src/native/actions.rs:1700-1727 (event subscription + auto_handled skip for beforeunload/alert), :2411-2450 (fail-fast error text + safe_during_dialog allowlist), :7258-7300 (dialog status/accept/dismiss + pending_pointer_release), :3888-3896 (autosave skipped while a dialog is pending); cli/src/native/browser.rs:1642-1647 (dialogBlocked flag on tab switch); cli/src/native/cdp/types.rs:212-228 (JavascriptDialogOpeningEvent / HandleJavaScriptDialogParams); cli/src/flags.rs:1001 (--no-auto-dialog). cuttle: internal/serve/wsproxy.go:246-275 (sendInjected/pinPage hook), internal/serve/humanize.go:782-850, :425-475.
cuttle_gaps.risk: Auto-dismissing beforeunload changes observable behavior a site could fingerprint (a real user takes ~1s to click 'Leave'). Coherence-preserving variant: route the auto-dismiss through the humanizer's own timing - sleep a log-normal human decision delay (reuse prePressDwell/clickHold distributions) before injecting handleJavaScriptDialog, rather than answering in <1ms. Page.enable itself is a per-session DevTools flag with no page-observable surface, same class as the Emulation.setFocusEmulationEnabled pin cuttle already injects.

cuttle_gaps.gap: No verb in cuttle emits machine-readable output. Every command writes prose to stdout (renderBriefing in internal/cli/briefing.go, runStatus in commands.go:770-826, listDownloads' tab-separated lines at commands.go:967-986, context ls). An agent that wants the CDP URL, the running state, the image, or the download list has to regex human text that also carries multi-paragraph instructional prose - which it must re-read on every `up` and every `status`.
cuttle_gaps.what_to_build: Add a persistent `--json` flag on rootCmd (internal/cli/root.go) and thread it through a small output seam modelled on playwright-cli's Output interface: one `type out interface { briefing(briefing); status(statusData); downloads([]download); contexts([]ctx); fail(code string, msg string, data map[string]any) }` with textOut (today's renderers, unchanged) and jsonOut. Emit one JSON object per invocation. The status payload should be the union of what runStatus already knows (state, cdpURL, viewerURL, image, engine, ports, context, name) plus the drivers array detectDrivers() already builds (name, version, attach line, docs command) - i.e. the briefing as data instead of a 30-line paragraph.
cuttle_gaps.evidence: microsoft/playwright: packages/playwright-core/src/tools/cli-client/output.ts - `interface Output` with `readonly json: boolean`, `TextOutput`/`JsonOutput`, typed `ListedBrowser`/`ListData` payloads. vercel-labs/agent-browser: `--json` is a global flag on every command (skill-data/core/SKILL.md 'Global flags worth knowing'), and `doctor --json` / `session info --json` / `tab list --json` are the documented programmatic paths. cuttle: no --json anywhere (grepped every Use:/RunE in internal/cli/commands.go).
cuttle_gaps.risk: None to stealth. The real risk is surface duplication - guard it the way playwright-cli does, by making the interface the ONLY way anything is printed, so a new verb cannot ship text-only.

cuttle_gaps.gap: Errors carry no machine code and no recovery data. internal/cli/commands.go raises bare strings (:581 'running but CDP is not answering', :583 'started but CDP never came up', :781 'nothing running', :1008 'pull %q: %s (HTTP %d)', :75 errCDPNotAnswering) and runStatus prints a human block then returns the opaque errUnhealthy sentinel (:826). The daemon side is the same: internal/serve/http.go writes `{"error": "Invalid fingerprint seed"}`, `{"error": "no state for seed"}`, `{"error": "ETag mismatch"}` - a message string and nothing else. An agent cannot branch on failure class, and the retry it picks is a guess.
cuttle_gaps.what_to_build: Define a small closed set of codes in internal/cli and internal/serve and attach them at every raise site: `not_running`, `cdp_unreachable`, `port_shadowed`, `image_skew`, `seed_invalid`, `state_conflict`, `download_missing`, `backend_unsupported`, `dialog_blocked`. Under --json emit `{"error":{"code":"port_shadowed","message":"...","data":{"port":9222,"owner":"node","pid":4711},"fix":"cuttle up --cdp-port 9444"}}`; under text keep today's prose verbatim plus the fix line. Populate `data` with what the recovery actually needs - for port_shadowed the lsof owner cuttle's own SKILL.md gotcha #7 tells the agent to run by hand; for image_skew the container image vs cliVersion(); for cdp_unreachable the log tail Diagnostics() already produces.
cuttle_gaps.evidence: vercel-labs/agent-browser: cli/src/native/browser.rs:416 TAB_GONE_PREFIX and :1000 tab_gone_error(target_id, last_url); cli/src/native/actions.rs:11448 `resp["code"] = json!("tab_gone")`; documented contract in cli/src/output.rs:2433 'JSON output includes code=tab_gone, data.targetId, and an optional sanitized data.lastUrl'. microsoft/playwright: cli-client/output.ts - errorDetachNotAttached/errorBrowserNotOpenForTool each print the exact next command to run, in both text and JSON renderings.
cuttle_gaps.risk: None. The codes are a public contract, so keep the set small and additive-only.

cuttle_gaps.gap: cuttle's SKILL.md is a 489-line monolith with no install path, no drift detection, and no topic addressing. internal/cli/skill.go (31 lines) has exactly one behavior: write the whole embedded file to stdout - and SKILL.md itself forbids truncating it ('never pipe a docs command through head/tail/sed/grep'). So the agent's only options are 'load ~7k tokens' or 'load nothing'. There is also no way to plant the skill into a repo's .claude/skills/ or .agents/skills/, and no way to notice when a stale planted copy no longer matches the installed binary - the exact failure mode cuttle's own drivers.go was designed to prevent for OTHER tools' docs.
cuttle_gaps.what_to_build: Two changes to internal/cli/skill.go and internal/cli/SKILL.md. (1) Split the file: keep a ~180-line core (setup, attach-never-spawn, the briefing contract, humanize pacing, VNC handoff, the top gotchas) and move contexts/backends, persistence + named profiles, downloads, multi-seed farm, engine swap, and server deployment into embedded `references/*.md`. Serve them addressably: `cuttle skill` prints the core plus a 'Specific tasks' link list, `cuttle skill <topic>` prints one reference, `cuttle skill --full` prints everything - the exact shape of `agent-browser skills get core [--full]` and playwright-cli's references/ index. (2) Add `cuttle skill --install [--agents]` writing to ./.claude/skills/cuttle/ (or ./.agents/skills/cuttle/), and a drift check on `cuttle up`: byte-compare any installed copy against the embedded skillGuide and print a boxed warning naming the exact reinstall command when they differ.
cuttle_gaps.evidence: microsoft/playwright-cli: skillCheck.js (bundledSkillFile/installedSkillTargets/readSkill + boxed frame() warning, run from playwright-cli.js:52 on every non-install invocation); `playwright-cli install --skills` / `--skills=agents`; skills/playwright-cli/SKILL.md is 420 lines with nine references/*.md (2025 lines total) linked under 'Specific tasks'. vercel-labs/agent-browser: skills/agent-browser/SKILL.md is a 51-line `hidden: true` discovery stub whose body is 'This file is a discovery stub, not the usage guide'; real content is skill-data/core/SKILL.md (516 lines) + 10 references + 3 templates, served by cli/src/skills.rs via `skills list` / `skills get <name> [--full]`; AGENTS.md documents the split explicitly.
cuttle_gaps.risk: None to stealth. Splitting risks the agent skipping a reference it needed - mitigate the way playwright-cli does: keep every rule whose absence causes a WRONG action (attach-never-spawn, one-driver-at-a-time, secrets, the write-consent rule) in the core, and move only rules whose absence causes a MISSING capability into references.

cuttle_gaps.gap: cuttle has no self-diagnosis verb. Triage today is: read `cuttle status` prose, then read SKILL.md gotcha #7, then hand-run `lsof -nP -iTCP:<port> -sTCP:LISTEN`, then `curl /json/version` to confirm the engine, then `cuttle logs`. Every one of those checks is knowable programmatically and none of them is. The port-shadow case is the sharpest: cuttle's own docs admit `docker run` does NOT error when a native process already owns the host port, so `up` prints a mapping that is silently dead - and the CLI knows the port it published and could just check who is listening.
cuttle_gaps.what_to_build: Add `cuttle doctor [--json]` running an ordered check list, each `{name, ok, detail, fix}`, exit 0 when all pass / 1 on any failure: (1) backend reachable (docker/ssh/kubectl present and answering); (2) container state + image vs cliVersion() skew; (3) port ownership - is the listener on --cdp-port actually the container, or a native process shadowing it; (4) CDP identity - `/json/version` Browser string matches the expected stealth build, catching 'the driver is quietly on its own Chrome', the trap SKILL.md flags under 'Prove you are attached'; (5) VNC reachable on --vnc-port; (6) drivers - reuse detectDrivers(), report versions and which is default; (7) seed health - GET / and report per-seed pid/connections/timezone/locale/proxy; (8) /dev/shm size in the container (the documented --shm-size=2g crash cause). Gate anything destructive behind an explicit flag rather than doing it, per agent-browser's `--fix` split.
cuttle_gaps.evidence: vercel-labs/agent-browser: cli/src/doctor/ (launch.rs, webgpu.rs, ...) behind `doctor [--json] [--fix] [--offline] [--quick]`, documented in skill-data/core/SKILL.md as 'run doctor before anything else', auto-cleans stale socket/pid/version sidecars, exit 0 warnings-OK / 1 on fail. CloakHQ/CloakBrowser: cloakbrowser/__main__.py - `install|info|doctor|update|clear-cache`, with _binary_version() at :75-105 appending --no-startup-window on Windows because Chromium ignores --version there and a healthy install otherwise times out.
cuttle_gaps.risk: None to stealth - every probe is local or loopback. Keep it one file (internal/cli/doctor.go) and resist a check-plugin abstraction; the checks are a fixed list.

cuttle_gaps.gap: The agent cannot see the seed's identity, so it cannot tell a deliberate design choice from a bug - which is the root of reported pain #1. chromePool.status() (internal/serve/pool.go) already returns per-seed pid/port/seed/connections/timezone/locale/proxy over `GET /`, but that endpoint appears nowhere in SKILL.md, has no CLI verb, and omits the two fields that would end the confusion: the seed's spoofed screen size (computed by ScreenArgs/screenChoices in internal/fingerprint/args.go:315-373) and the resulting --window-size. An agent looking at a browser window occupying part of a 1920x1080 VNC framebuffer has no way to learn the window is correctly sized to a spoofed 1366x768 screen, so it reports a bug or tries to 'fix' it. Egress IP is likewise invisible, so the agent cannot check the proxy/timezone coherence SKILL.md tells it to care about.
cuttle_gaps.what_to_build: Extend chromePool.status() per-seed maps with `screen` ({width,height}), `window_size`, `persona` ({platform, arch}) and a lazily-probed, cached `egress_ip`; document `GET /` in SKILL.md next to the /downloads section; surface it as `cuttle status --json` (folding into gap 2) and add one line to the text briefing: `seed default  1366x768 screen in a 1920x1080 viewer (by design)`. Keep the egress probe out of the hot path - probe on demand only, through the seed's own page so it goes through the seed's proxy.
cuttle_gaps.evidence: clearcotelabs/clearcote-browser: mcp/clearcote_mcp/server.py - `get_egress_info` ('Report the browser's public egress IP (through any configured proxy) + the active persona') and `get_cdp_endpoint`, which returns the endpoint plus a `connect` dict of ready-to-paste snippets for playwright_python / playwright_node / puppeteer / browser_use. CloakHQ/CloakBrowser-Manager: backend/main.py:602 GET /api/status returns a typed StatusResponse (running_count, binary_version, license_tier, host_os, runtime_mode, viewer_mode, windows_fonts_present/required/complete) - environment truth as data, including a font-completeness health flag. cuttle: internal/serve/pool.go chromePool.status(), internal/fingerprint/args.go:315-373.
cuttle_gaps.risk: Adding an egress-IP probe means the daemon makes an outbound request the seed did not ask for. Coherence-preserving variant: run it in the seed's own page context via CDP (so it carries the seed's proxy, TLS stack, and headers) rather than from Go's http.Client, which would egress with the daemon's fingerprint and, on a proxied seed, from the wrong IP entirely. Cache it per seed and never probe on a timer.

cuttle_gaps.gap: Secret handling is delegated entirely to one driver and does not survive the batching advice cuttle itself gives. SKILL.md's secrets rule depends on `PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_SECRETS_FILE` - a playwright-cli-only mechanism - and then admits its own hole: the substitution 'does not reach a scripted eval/run-code block, whose sandbox has no process.env, so a batched script can only hold a secret by inlining the literal value into its argv - where redaction, which only rewrites command OUTPUT, can never reach it.' agent-browser and browser-use users get nothing at all. Meanwhile cuttle sits at the CDP layer where every keystroke passes through code it owns (handleInsertText already rewrites Input.insertText into real keystrokes, internal/serve/humanize.go:570-666), and it has a KasmVNC session where the clipboard is a legitimate transport - and uses neither. This is reported pain #2.
cuttle_gaps.what_to_build: Two complementary pieces, both driver-agnostic because they live below the driver. (1) Proxy-level substitution + redaction: add `cuttle secret put <NAME>` (value read from stdin, never argv, stored daemon-side per seed, never persisted to the state store) and in internal/serve/wsproxy.go's preprocessClient expand the literal token `{{NAME}}` inside Input.insertText / Input.dispatchKeyEvent text params before the humanizer rewrites it into keystrokes - so the agent types `{{GH_TOKEN}}` and the real value exists only inside the daemon. Symmetrically, redact every stored value out of forwarded browser->client frames the way playwright's redactSecrets does, replacing it with `<secret>NAME</secret>`. This closes the eval/run-code hole automatically: an eval that reads the field back gets the placeholder. (2) Clipboard transport for the VNC path: add `POST /clipboard?fingerprint=<seed>` running xclip on the seed's DISPLAY (the container already runs Xvfb/openbox), so a human-handoff login or a paste-only field works without the value ever entering the transcript.
cuttle_gaps.evidence: microsoft/playwright: packages/playwright-core/src/tools/backend/context.ts:346-372 (lookupSecret + redactSecrets doing text.replaceAll(secretValue, `<secret>${name}</secret>`)), applied at backend/response.ts:220 (tool responses), :119 (files written), backend/logFile.ts:94 (session log); loaded via tools/mcp/config.ts:444 PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_SECRETS_FILE and tools/mcp/program.ts:70 --secrets; tests/mcp/secrets.spec.ts covers redaction in the console-log artifact (microsoft/playwright#41509). CloakHQ/CloakBrowser-Manager: backend/main.py:641 POST /api/profiles/{id}/clipboard (xclip -selection clipboard on the profile's DISPLAY, killing the prior xclip first since it stays alive to serve paste) and :677 GET, which reads back via Playwright's window.__clipboardText because Chrome under KasmVNC never writes to the X11 clipboard.
cuttle_gaps.risk: Redaction that rewrites forwarded CDP frames must never corrupt binary/screenshot payloads - scope the replaceAll to text frames and skip Page.captureScreenshot/Network body results. Stealth-wise the substitution is free: the value still goes out as real humanized keystrokes, identical bytes on the wire. The clipboard path is the one with a behavioral cost - a paste fires no keydown sequence, and some login forms fingerprint that. Coherence-preserving variant: default the clipboard endpoint to human handoff (the operator pastes it in the viewer) and keep {{NAME}} keystroke substitution as the automation path, so an automated fill is always a real typing sequence.

cuttle_gaps.gap: No screenshot path of cuttle's own, and the driver's screenshot answers a different question than the one the agent is asking. SKILL.md correctly warns that driver-written files land on the DRIVER daemon's host, not in the container - but that leaves the agent with no way to see the VNC framebuffer, which is the only view that includes the native Chrome dialog stacked over the page (Page.captureScreenshot is renderer-only and shows nothing of a beforeunload prompt). So when pain #4 happens, the agent's screenshot looks fine and the page still will not respond. This is reported pain #3 plus half of #4.
cuttle_gaps.what_to_build: Mirror the downloads verb exactly, which is already the right shape (content never touches stdout, 0600, prints only a path). Add `GET /screenshot?fingerprint=<seed>[&framebuffer=1]` in internal/serve/http.go routes(): default does Page.captureScreenshot on the seed's active tab over its loopback CDP; `framebuffer=1` grabs the X display instead (the image already runs Xvfb - an `xwd`/ffmpeg one-shot on the seed's DISPLAY), which is what shows native dialogs, the window-vs-framebuffer geometry, and anything openbox drew. Add `cuttle screenshot [dest]` writing 0600 and printing only the local path, working over the ssh/k8s tunnels for free since it rides the same HTTP surface as downloads.
cuttle_gaps.evidence: microsoft/playwright-cli: skills/playwright-cli/SKILL.md 'Save as' section (`screenshot [ref] [--filename] [--hires]`, `pdf --filename`) plus the note that snapshot is normally preferred over screenshot. vercel-labs/agent-browser: `screenshot --annotate map.png` - 'numbered labels + legend keyed to snapshot refs... designed for multimodal models: each label [N] maps to ref @eN'; also `screenshot` is on the safe_during_dialog allowlist (cli/src/native/actions.rs:2432) precisely because it is how you SEE a dialog. clearcotelabs/clearcote-browser: mcp/clearcote_mcp/server.py screenshot_page/save_page_pdf confined via _confine_path to a sandbox write root. cuttle: internal/serve/downloads.go + internal/cli/commands.go:990-1024 pullDownload is the pattern to copy.
cuttle_gaps.risk: Adding an ffmpeg/xwd dependency to the runtime image for the framebuffer mode is real image weight. Coherence-preserving variant: ship the CDP screenshot first (zero new deps, covers most needs), and add framebuffer capture only if KasmVNC's existing stack already exposes a frame grab - it is a viewer, so check before adding a binary. No stealth surface either way; Page.captureScreenshot is not page-observable.

cuttle_gaps.gap: The auth-state checkpoint has no known-good guard, so a transient logged-out read can silently overwrite a good login. supervise.go doCapture() carries forward localStorage for origins whose tab is gone (profile.CarryForward, supervise.go:162-172) - good - but a SUCCESSFUL extract that legitimately returns zero cookies is written straight through via store.put (supervise.go:131). That is precisely the false-negative cuttle's own SKILL.md gotcha #4 warns agents about ('a cookie read that returns zero cookies is usually the driver probing its own blank page'), and the daemon does not apply its own warning to itself. The checkpoint fires on last-client-detach, on a backstop timer, and at shutdown, so a seed that is mid-redirect or momentarily on about:blank at one of those moments can clobber the snapshot that `cuttle down` and box-loss recovery depend on.
cuttle_gaps.what_to_build: Add a save policy to the store put path in internal/serve/state.go / supervise.go: refuse to persist a capture that has strictly fewer cookie DOMAINS than the prior snapshot unless the seed was explicitly PUT (Supervised) with the new state, log it at warn with the existing stateSummary() counts on both sides, and keep the prior snapshot. Optionally expose a per-seed restore predicate on the PUT API (a required cookie domain, or a required text on a probe URL) so a caller can declare what 'logged in' means for that seed. This is one guard clause plus a log line; it does not need a policy enum unless a second caller appears.
cuttle_gaps.evidence: vercel-labs/agent-browser: `--restore-save <auto|always|never>` with skill-data/core/SKILL.md stating 'Use --restore-save auto by default so a failed restore does not overwrite the previous known-good state'; `--restore-check-text Dashboard` as an explicit restore-validity predicate; periodic autosave throttled by AGENT_BROWSER_AUTOSAVE_INTERVAL_MS with a quiet period (cli/src/native/actions.rs:3878-3905 autosave_due, which also refuses to run while a dialog is pending). cuttle: internal/serve/supervise.go:116-140 doCapture, :162-172 extractSeedState/CarryForward, internal/serve/state.go stateStore.put.
cuttle_gaps.risk: A legitimate logout would now fail to persist as a logout, leaving a stale cookie set that gets re-injected on next launch. Coherence-preserving variant: the guard is one-directional and overridable - an explicit PUT /profile/{seed}/state (the deliberate-discard path, which `cuttle down --purge` and purge-profile already use) always writes through; only the automatic checkpoint is guarded.

cuttle_gaps.gap: cuttle offers no per-command timeout or error boundary of its own at the CDP proxy layer, so a wedged operation surfaces as a hang rather than a typed failure. The humanizer withholds a driver's ack while it runs verifyToggle (humanize.go:463-475) and awaitStable can loop up to gateMaxRetries with growing backoff - all with no ceiling reported to the caller and no way to distinguish 'humanize pacing, be patient' (which SKILL.md explicitly tells the agent not to treat as a hang) from 'genuinely stuck'. The agent is told to wait, so it waits through real failures too.
cuttle_gaps.what_to_build: Give the humanizer's withheld-ack paths a hard wall-clock budget (the sum of gate + toggle budgets is already bounded by constants - just enforce it as one deadline) and, on expiry, answer the driver's command with a CDP error carrying a cuttle-specific message naming what timed out ('cuttle: pre-click settle gate exceeded 2s at (x,y); the page may be blocked by a dialog or still animating'). Surface the same fact structurally in the /dialogs endpoint from gap 1 so an agent that sees a slow click has one place to check why.
cuttle_gaps.evidence: clearcotelabs/clearcote-browser: mcp/clearcote_mcp/server.py `_safe` decorator - 'Per-tool wall-clock timeout + structured error, so a bad/slow call never wedges the server', asyncio.wait_for(timeout=CLEARCOTE_MCP_TOOL_TIMEOUT default 90) returning {'status':'error','error':'tool timed out after Ns (raise CLEARCOTE_MCP_TOOL_TIMEOUT for slow pages)'}, plus a catch-all at the tool boundary. vercel-labs/agent-browser: cli/src/native/actions.rs:2441 turns a renderer-blocked page into an immediate typed error naming the blocker and the retry, rather than letting the client read-timeout. cuttle: internal/serve/humanize.go:99-112 (togglePollBudget/gateBackoff constants), :463-475 (withheld ack).
cuttle_gaps.risk: Answering with an error where cuttle previously answered ok changes driver-visible behavior and could abort a flow that would have succeeded a beat later. Coherence-preserving variant: keep failing OPEN (still dispatch the click) and make the timeout an ADVISORY - forward the driver's normal ok response but emit the timeout fact to /dialogs and the daemon log, so nothing that works today breaks and the agent gains a place to look.

cuttle_gaps.gap: No decision is recorded on MCP-vs-CLI, and the CLI's own machine surface is thin enough that a wrapper cannot be written cleanly. Two of the six comparison repos ship MCP servers (clearcote's minimal one, agent-browser's profile-paginated one with a written CLI/MCP parity contract), so the question will be asked. cuttle's KISS/YAGNI non-negotiable argues against building one - but that argument only holds if the CLI is machine-consumable, which today it is not.
cuttle_gaps.what_to_build: Do NOT ship an MCP server - it is a second surface to keep in parity for a tool whose whole model is 'attach your own driver', and cuttle's briefing/driver-registry design is already the better answer for that. Instead, close the two things MCP would have bought and say so in SKILL.md: (a) machine-readable output (gaps 2 and 3 above), which makes cuttle wrappable by whoever wants MCP; (b) copy clearcote's get_cdp_endpoint payload shape into `cuttle status --json` - emit the attach commands as a `drivers[].attach` array (detectDrivers already builds exactly this, internal/cli/drivers.go:47-72) plus a `connect` map of raw-library snippets for playwright-python/playwright-node/puppeteer/browser-use, so an agent using a library rather than one of the three registered driver CLIs gets a correct line instead of the single hardcoded chromium.connectOverCDP example in SKILL.md.
cuttle_gaps.evidence: vercel-labs/agent-browser: AGENTS.md 'CLI/MCP Parity' section - every CLI change must update cli/src/mcp.rs in the same change, with tests proving alignment; cli/src/mcp.rs is 151KB / 4367 lines, and tool discovery is paginated into profiles (core/network/state/debug/tabs/react/mobile/all) purely to keep MCP context small. clearcotelabs/clearcote-browser: mcp/clearcote_mcp/server.py get_cdp_endpoint returns cdp_url plus a connect dict with playwright_python / playwright_node / puppeteer / browser_use snippets, documented as 'the whole point of the drop-in model'; ToolAnnotations(readOnlyHint/openWorldHint) per tool. cuttle: internal/cli/drivers.go (registry with attach templates + per-driver docs command), internal/cli/SKILL.md 'Raw CDP libraries work too' (one snippet, node only).
cuttle_gaps.risk: None. This is explicitly the anti-build recommendation - the risk is the opposite one, of adding an MCP server that duplicates the CLI and drifts, which agent-browser needs a written contract and a test suite to prevent.

themes.theme: Stealth capability gaps: engine patch coverage, CDP-detectability, and network-layer leaks
themes.state_of_the_art:
Three different postures, and cuttle sits behind all three in different places.

**clark-labs-inc/clark-browser** (cuttle's fork parent) is honest about what is spec vs. shipped: `PATCHES.md:124` marks patch #38 (`--fingerprint-webrtc-ip` replaces the ICE host candidate) as status "spec", NOT implemented. What clark actually ships for WebRTC is a *launcher* policy - `clarkbrowser/browser.py:_cohere_webrtc_policy_args()` auto-emits `--force-webrtc-ip-handling-policy=disable_non_proxied_udp` + `--webrtc-ip-handling-policy=disable_non_proxied_udp` whenever a proxy is configured, documented in `specs/I-webrtc.md` as RFC 8828 Mode 4. Since the stealth5 tag clark added two patches: `0027-analyser-node-noise.patch` (seed-derived per-bin noise in `realtime_analyser.cc` on `getFloatFrequencyData`/`getByteFrequencyData`, because a site reading the frequency domain via AnalyserNode bypasses patch #26's AudioBuffer noise entirely) and `0047-suppress-cdc-globals.patch` (a v8::Extension that pre-defines `cdc_*`/`__webdriver*`/`__selenium*` as non-configurable undefined and monkey-patches `Object.defineProperty` to reject them).

**clearcotelabs/clearcote-browser** is the most advanced engine work of the three. `patches/110-runtime-enable.patch` is the only in-engine fix for the `Runtime.enable` CDP leak anywhere in this set: it early-returns from `V8RuntimeAgentImpl::addBindings`, hard-codes `enabled() { return false; }`, and comments out `if (m_enabled) reportMessage(message, true)` in `messageAdded` - killing the console-serialization path that fires a page-supplied `Error.stack` getter. Their `sdk/node/src/launchopts.ts` carries the sharpest published field report on WebRTC: `webrtcDefaultDenyArgs()` was added because a customer with "an otherwise perfectly coherent persona" was flagged for location spoofing - a page setting `iceTransportPolicy:"relay"` forces its own TURN server, TURN prefers UDP, an HTTP/SOCKS proxy carries only TCP, so the UDP left on the host's own path and the TURN server read the real public address straight off the packet, *no candidate involved, so fabricating one changed nothing*. 0.27.0 (`da07119`) adds a real SOCKS5 UDP-ASSOCIATE relay behind `--socks5-udp` as the non-lossy alternative. `docs/PATCHES.md` states two rules cuttle violates: the **render-backend rule** ("Never advertise a discrete NVIDIA-class renderer over a backend that does not produce that GPU's pixels... a string spoof that creates a renderer-vs-readPixels mismatch makes the browser *more* detectable than shipping the backend's honest string"; on a SwiftShader runtime, advertise an ANGLE-SwiftShader-consistent string) and **never blank** ("empty `getVoices()`, blank canvas, zeroed readPixels - each is a *harder* tell than the real value"). `patches/050-shadow-dom.patch` shows exactly how ungoogled's client-rects noise is implemented and deletes it: `noise_factor_x_/y_ = 1 + (base::RandDouble()-0.5)*0.000003` set in the `Document` constructor - a fresh random factor per document, unrelated to any seed. Their whole thesis (`docs/PATCHES.md` §1.2) is that one global `--fingerprint` int is a cross-site linking supercookie, replaced by Brave-style per-eTLD+1 derivation from a session token.

**CloakHQ/CloakBrowser** contributes the operational discipline rather than readable patches (binary is proprietary). `js/src/config.ts:409` ships `IGNORE_DEFAULT_ARGS = ["--enable-automation", "--enable-unsafe-swiftshader"]` with the reasoning inline. Their binary *does* implement `--fingerprint-webrtc-ip` (README flags table, auto-injected by `geoip=True`) and QUIC-over-SOCKS5 UDP ASSOCIATE (`README.md:165`), plus `--fingerprint-sapi-voices` for the Windows speech-voice roster and `--enable-blink-features=FakeShadowRoot` for closed shadow DOM. Most importantly `CHANGELOG.md:131`: their Docker smoke gates on Sannysoft, Incolumitas, **Rebrowser**, deviceandbrowserinfo, BrowserScan, and **CreepJS lies/noise=false** - an external adversarial suite, not a self-authored expectation set.

**Drivers** contribute nothing here: neither `microsoft/playwright-cli` nor `vercel-labs/agent-browser` has any Runtime.enable mitigation (greps for `Runtime.enable`/`createIsolatedWorld` in `cli/src/*.rs` return nothing), so upstream playwright-core's unconditional `Runtime.enable` per context reaches cuttle's binary as-is. rebrowser documents this vector as "used by all major anti-bot software such as Cloudflare, DataDome". Because cuttle is the multiplexer, it is the only layer that can fix it once for all three drivers.

cuttle_gaps.gap: cuttle's WebRTC exit-IP spoof is a no-op. `--fingerprint-webrtc-ip=<exitIP>` is declared in packages/browser/patches/000-shared/clark_fingerprint_switches.{h,cc} and whitelisted into the renderer in 0050-renderer-arg-whitelist-fingerprint.patch:71, but NO patch in the series reads it. cuttle spends a live network round-trip through the proxy to resolve the exit IP (internal/serve/pool.go:344-374, internal/fingerprint/geoip.go) and passes a flag the binary ignores. No `--force-webrtc-ip-handling-policy` is emitted either, so in the container ICE enumerates the host's own interfaces and STUN produces a srflx candidate from the real (non-proxy) egress path.
cuttle_gaps.what_to_build: Two-part. (1) Zero-build fix in internal/serve/pool.go, in the same block that appends --fingerprint-webrtc-ip: when `proxy != ""`, also append `--force-webrtc-ip-handling-policy=disable_non_proxied_udp` and `--webrtc-ip-handling-policy=disable_non_proxied_udp` unless the caller already set either key (BuildArgs dedupes on the pre-`=` key, so a caller override wins naturally). Snapshot it in internal/fingerprint/testdata/golden.json via `just parity-golden` so the pairing is a tripwire. (2) Decide the flag's fate: either implement patch 0038 against `third_party/webrtc/rtc_base/network.cc` `BasicNetworkManager::CreateNetworks` per clark's specs/I-webrtc.md (clear the enumerated networks, push one ADAPTER_TYPE_ETHERNET network at the spoofed IP), or delete `--fingerprint-webrtc-ip` from pool.go plus the exit-IP resolution that feeds it, and correct docs/STEALTH-VERIFICATION.md:36 and the geoip.go:129 comment that both claim it works today.
cuttle_gaps.evidence: clark-labs-inc/clark-browser PATCHES.md:124 marks #38 status "spec" (unimplemented); clark's shipped mitigation is clarkbrowser/browser.py:_cohere_webrtc_policy_args() + specs/I-webrtc.md. clearcotelabs/clearcote-browser sdk/node/src/launchopts.ts:webrtcDefaultDenyArgs() plus the ~20-line comment above it describing a real customer flagged for location spoofing via iceTransportPolicy:"relay"/TURN reading the real public IP off the UDP packet. CloakHQ/CloakBrowser README.md:732 (binary implements the switch for real).
cuttle_gaps.risk: disable_non_proxied_udp genuinely breaks peer connections that need UDP, and denying non-proxied UDP is itself a (much weaker) behavioral signal. Coherence-preserving variant: gate it on `proxy != ""` only - that is exactly when the leak exists - and leave direct sessions on stock behavior, which is what both clark and clearcote settled on. The bigger stealth-coherence risk is the status quo: cuttle currently ships a documented guarantee it does not deliver, so a proxied seed's WebRTC egress contradicts its own geoip timezone/locale.

cuttle_gaps.gap: No mitigation for the `Runtime.enable` CDP leak - the single most widely deployed CDP-detection vector. internal/serve/wsproxy.go intercepts only Target.createBrowserContext, Fetch.enable/authRequired, Emulation.setLocaleOverride and Emulation.setFocusEmulationEnabled; `Runtime.enable` passes straight through from every driver, and no engine patch neutralizes the observable side effect (console-message serialization firing a page-installed `Error.prototype.stack` getter).
cuttle_gaps.what_to_build: Prefer the engine fix, but NOT clearcote's blunt form. Narrow variant: in v8/src/inspector, keep `messageAdded`/`reportMessage` alive but stop the page-observable read - report console messages with `generatePreview=false` and build the stack from the `v8::StackTrace` captured at message creation rather than reading the argument object's `stack` accessor. That closes rebrowser's runtimeEnableLeak while `Runtime.consoleAPICalled` and `Runtime.bindingCalled` keep working. Add it as packages/browser/patches/0052-runtime-enable-no-accessor-leak.patch and assert it in packages/browser/validate/smoke.py against the published detector snippet (getter on `stack` + `console.debug`). If the engine route is rejected, the multiplexer route is cuttle's unique leverage: in wsproxy.go swallow the driver's `Runtime.enable`, reply `{}` success, and synthesize `Runtime.executionContextCreated` for the driver from `Page.createIsolatedWorld` + `Runtime.addBinding` (rebrowser's addBinding mode) - one fix that covers playwright-cli, agent-browser and browser-use simultaneously.
cuttle_gaps.evidence: clearcotelabs/clearcote-browser patches/110-runtime-enable.patch (early-return in V8RuntimeAgentImpl::addBindings, `enabled(){return false;}`, commented-out `if (m_enabled) reportMessage(message,true)`). rebrowser/rebrowser-patches README and rebrowser.net/blog/how-to-fix-runtime-enable-cdp-detection... document the technique as used by Cloudflare and DataDome; rebrowser-bot-detector's `runtimeEnableLeak` test is the check. Neither microsoft/playwright-cli nor vercel-labs/agent-browser carries any mitigation (no Runtime.enable/createIsolatedWorld hits in cli/src/*.rs).
cuttle_gaps.risk: Copying clearcote's patch verbatim is a functional regression, not just a stealth trade: killing `addBindings` breaks Playwright `exposeFunction`/`exposeBinding` (Runtime.bindingCalled), and killing `messageAdded` breaks `page.on('console')` - which agents rely on for debugging, and which cuttle's own humanize layer does not replace. The narrow variant above keeps both. The wsproxy variant risks execution-context-id mismatches inside playwright-core, so it needs the smoke harness in test/smoke/ extended before it can ship.

cuttle_gaps.gap: cuttle enables ungoogled-chromium's client-rects / canvas noise, whose noise factor is a fresh `base::RandDouble()` per Document, not derived from `--fingerprint`. internal/fingerprint/args.go:203-205 passes --fingerprinting-client-rects-noise, --fingerprinting-canvas-measuretext-noise and --fingerprinting-canvas-image-data-noise. Consequence: getBoundingClientRect/getClientRects sub-pixel values differ on every page load and per iframe within the same persona - a real browser holds them rock-stable. That is a flicker tell, and it is scored directly by CreepJS as noise/lies.
